note: Hand-checked builds. Every entry links to where it came from; perk names are resolved against live game data at each sync and a build is dropped if a perk no longer exists.

builds.title: The Most Requested Legion Build
builds.summary: Basic-attack downs explode every generator within {{Surge|affecteddistance}} m, and after each hook you can press the ability button to explode one generator you can see within {{Turn Back The Clock|range}} m.
builds.details: Surge: whenever you down a Survivor with a basic attack, every generator within {{Surge|affecteddistance}} m explodes, loses {{Surge|regression%}}% progress and starts regressing, and Survivors repairing it scream. Turn Back the Clock: for {{Turn Back The Clock|duration}} s after hooking a Survivor you can press the ability button to make one generator you can see within {{Turn Back The Clock|range}} m explode, lose {{Turn Back The Clock|generatorregression%}}% progress and start regressing. The other two perks pay off as Survivors finish generators. Batteries Included gives you {{Batteries Included|haste%}}% Haste while you are within {{Batteries Included|requireddistance}} m of a completed generator, ending {{Batteries Included|hastelingerduration}} s after you leave. Each completed generator also earns {{Coup de Grace|tokensgainedpergenerator}} Coup de Grâce Tokens (up to {{Coup de Grace|maxtokens}}); every lunge spends one automatically to make that lunge {{Coup de Grace|lungeextraduration%}}% longer.
tips: Surge only counts downs made with a basic attack, so try to finish chases close to generators that are being repaired.
After each hook, look for a generator in sight within {{Turn Back The Clock|range}} m before you walk away: you have {{Turn Back The Clock|duration}} s to press the ability button.
Batteries Included only works within {{Batteries Included|requireddistance}} m of a completed generator, so route chases past finished generators.
Coup de Grâce spends a Token on every lunge automatically, so the extra reach arrives right after a generator is completed and is used up on your next lunges.

builds.title: Gate-Lock Endgame (NOED + Blood Warden)
builds.summary: None of this pays off before the last generator is done; then No One Escapes Death makes Survivors Exposed, No Way Out and Remember Me keep the gates shut longer, and Blood Warden can block both exits.
builds.details: When all generators are completed, No One Escapes Death lights a Dull Totem that makes Survivors Exposed and gives you {{Hex: No One Escapes Death|haste%}}% Haste, but Survivors within {{Hex: No One Escapes Death|aurarevealstartrange}} m see the totem's Aura, a range that grows to {{Hex: No One Escapes Death|aurarevealendrange}} m over {{Hex: No One Escapes Death|aurasizeincreasedelay}} s. No Way Out earns a Token the first time you hook each Survivor; after the last generator, when a Survivor starts opening an Exit Gate it is blocked for {{No Way Out|gateblockbaseduration}} s plus {{No Way Out|gateblockdurationpertoken}} s per Token and you are alerted. Remember Me earns a Token (up to {{Remember Me|maximumtokens}}) whenever the Obsession takes damage, and each Token makes every Survivor except the Obsession open Exit Gates {{Remember Me|actionspeedpenalty%}}% slower. Once an Exit Gate has been opened, your next hook triggers Blood Warden (once per trial), blocking both exits for {{Blood Warden|gateblockduration}} s, and Blood Warden also shows you the Auras of Survivors inside the exit thresholds, so a lost generator phase can still end in kills at the gates.
tips: Hook each Survivor once before the generators are done: No Way Out only earns a Token for the first hook on each Survivor.
Damage the Obsession whenever it is convenient to build Remember Me Tokens; each one makes every Survivor except the Obsession open Exit Gates {{Remember Me|actionspeedpenalty%}}% slower.
Blood Warden needs a hook after an Exit Gate has been opened and only works once per trial, so save a down for after a gate has been opened.
The creator names None Are Free as a swap for No Way Out.
builds.evidence: NightLight.gg community stats (patch window 10.1.0 onward, 2026-08-25 to 2026-11-16): #16 most-used killer build, 43 recorded loadouts (0.15% of all killer loadouts); 44 of 84 tracked survivors killed (52.4% kill rate).

builds.title: Silent Endgame
builds.summary: When the last generator is done Silent Shadow makes you Undetectable, Terminus makes the injured Broken, and No Way Out plus Remember Me keep Survivors at the gates longer.
builds.details: Silent Shadow makes you Undetectable for {{Silent Shadow|starttrialundetectableduration}} s whenever you hook a Survivor, and once all generators are completed it makes you Undetectable again, so Survivors on an Exit Gate do not get your Terror Radius as a warning. When all generators are completed, Terminus gives Broken to every injured, downed and hooked Survivor, ending {{Terminus|brokenduration}} s after an Exit Gate is opened. No Way Out earns a Token for the first hook on each Survivor and, after the last generator, blocks an Exit Gate for {{No Way Out|gateblockbaseduration}} s plus {{No Way Out|gateblockdurationpertoken}} s per Token when a Survivor starts opening it, while each Remember Me Token (earned whenever the Obsession takes damage) makes the other Survivors open gates {{Remember Me|actionspeedpenalty%}}% slower. Survivors get no Terror Radius warning while the gates stay blocked, which is what makes it so frustrating to face.
tips: The creator names None Are Free as an alternative to No Way Out.
The video runs it on The Slasher, The Hillbilly and The Krasue.
Terminus only affects Survivors who are injured, downed or hooked, so leave Survivors injured going into the endgame.
Before the endgame, walk away from each hook during Silent Shadow's {{Silent Shadow|starttrialundetectableduration}} s of Undetectable.

builds.title: Fake Hex Bait (Devour Hope + Pentimento)
builds.summary: Four Hexes where cleansing is the trap: Devour Hope grows while you stay away from unhooks, and Pentimento lets you rekindle cleansed totems into a heal and repair penalty for every Survivor.
builds.details: Devour Hope earns a Token whenever a Survivor is unhooked while you are at least {{Hex: Devour Hope|distancefromhook}} m away: at {{Hex: Devour Hope|tokensforhaste}} Tokens you gain {{Hex: Devour Hope|haste%}}% Haste for {{Hex: Devour Hope|hasteduration}} s starting {{Hex: Devour Hope|hastedelayduration}} s after each hook, at {{Hex: Devour Hope|tokensforexposed}} Tokens Survivors are Exposed, and at {{Hex: Devour Hope|tokensformori}} Tokens you can kill downed Survivors. Plaything hexes each Survivor the first time you hook them and lights a Dull Totem that is blocked for other Survivors for {{Hex: Plaything|totemblockduration}} s; the hexed Survivor is Oblivious and sees that totem's Aura within {{Hex: Plaything|totemaurarevealdistance}} m. Undying hands its own totem to the first other Hex that is cleansed or blessed, keeping that Hex's Tokens, but that may be a Plaything totem rather than Devour Hope. With Pentimento you see cleansed totems and can rekindle each once, and while a totem is rekindled Survivors heal and repair {{Hex: Pentimento|baseactionspeedpenalty%}}% slower, plus {{Hex: Pentimento|actionspeedpenaltypertotem%}}% for each additional rekindled totem.
tips: Walk at least {{Hex: Devour Hope|distancefromhook}} m away from each hook: Devour Hope only earns Tokens for unhooks that happen while you are that far away.

Every Hex needs its own totem and Devour Hope and Undying already take two of the trial's limited totems, so Plaything can only light on Dull Totems that are still free, and on fewer once Survivors cleanse them.
Rekindle cleansed totems along your patrol route; Survivors within {{Hex: Pentimento|totemaurareveadistance}} m can see a rekindled totem's Aura.

builds.title: Haunted Ground Totem Trap
builds.summary: Ruin, Thrill of the Hunt and Dominance make it look as if you are guarding a Hex, but cleansing either Haunted Ground totem makes every Survivor Exposed for {{Hex: Haunted Ground|exposedduration}} s.
builds.details: Haunted Ground lights two Dull Totems at the start of the trial; when either is cleansed or blessed, all Survivors become Exposed for {{Hex: Haunted Ground|exposedduration}} s and the other totem goes out. Ruin lights a totem too and makes every generator that is not being repaired regress at {{Hex: Ruin|regressionspeed%}}% speed, which gives Survivors a real reason to hunt totems. Thrill of the Hunt lights its totem on your first hook, and each hook then blocks all Hex Totems for {{Hex: Thrill of the Hunt|blockdurationpertoken}} s per lit Hex Totem. Dominance blocks each totem for {{Dominance|blockduration}} s the first time a Survivor starts blessing or cleansing it, and that Survivor screams and you see their Aura for {{Dominance|auraduration}} s.
tips: Dominance's scream and Aura show you who just started on a totem, so head that way and be near Survivors, not the totem, when a Haunted Ground breaks.
Only one Haunted Ground can go off: cleansing or blessing one extinguishes the other.
Haunted Ground and Ruin light three totems at the start, so Thrill of the Hunt needs a Dull Totem to still be free at your first hook.
Thrill of the Hunt and Dominance block the Haunted Ground totems too, so they delay the trap as well as protecting Ruin.

builds.title: 40-Metre Misery (terror-radius anti-heal)
builds.summary: Distressing stretches your Terror Radius, inside which Coulrophobia slows healing and Unnerving Presence shrinks skill checks, while Thanatophobia slows repairs, cleansing and sabotage for each Survivor left injured.
builds.details: Distressing makes your Terror Radius {{Distressing|terrorradiusincreasesize}}% larger and slows repairs inside it by {{Distressing|repairspeedpenalty}}%. Within that radius Coulrophobia makes Survivors heal {{Coulrophobia|healpenalty%}}% slower and spins their basic skill checks {{Coulrophobia|skillcheckspeedincrease%}}% faster while they heal, and Unnerving Presence gives them {{Unnerving Presence|skillcheckoddsincrease%}}% more basic skill checks, on top of making the good zone of basic skill checks {{Unnerving Presence|successzonesizepenalty%}}% smaller. Survivors who stay injured instead feed Thanatophobia, which slows repairs, totem cleansing and hook sabotage by {{Thanatophobia|actionspeedpenaltypersurvivor%}}% for each injured, downed or hooked Survivor, plus {{Thanatophobia|actionspeedpenaltybonus%}}% more once all four are.
tips: The creator recommends The Mastermind, The Blight and The Hillbilly, three of the killers with the largest base Terror Radius in the game data, which widens the area your Terror Radius perks cover.
Spread injuries before committing to a chase: Thanatophobia's extra penalty needs all four Survivors injured, downed or hooked at the same time.
Distressing's and Thanatophobia's repair penalties are the same kind of modifier, so Diminishing Returns reduces the smaller one instead of applying both in full.
Coulrophobia, Distressing's repair penalty and Unnerving Presence's extra skill checks only affect Survivors inside your Terror Radius, so stay near anyone healing or repairing.

builds.title: Never Healthy Again (universal anti-heal)
builds.summary: Spread injuries and keep them: Sloppy Butcher adds Mangled and Haemorrhage to basic-attack hits, Leverage slows healing after unhooks and Thanatophobia slows the team's repairs, cleansing and sabotage while they stay hurt.
builds.details: Every basic attack that damages a Survivor gives them Haemorrhage and Mangled from Sloppy Butcher, and Haemorrhage makes them lose healing progress faster. Leverage makes a Survivor who unhooks someone, or unhooks themselves, heal {{Leverage|healpenalty%}}% slower for {{Leverage|reducehealingduration}} s. Whenever a healthy Survivor becomes injured, Hysteria makes all injured Survivors Oblivious for {{Hysteria|obliviousduration}} s (cooldown {{Hysteria|cooldown}} s), and Thanatophobia slows repairs, totem cleansing and hook sabotage by {{Thanatophobia|actionspeedpenaltypersurvivor%}}% per injured, downed or hooked Survivor, plus {{Thanatophobia|actionspeedpenaltybonus%}}% once all four are. It rewards hit-and-run play: injure, move on and let the penalties pile up.
tips: Works on any killer; strongest on killers who can injure several Survivors quickly.
Sloppy Butcher only applies when a basic attack does the damage, so use basic attacks to spread it.
Oblivious Survivors do not perceive your Terror Radius, so right after Hysteria triggers, approach the other injured Survivors.
Go after the Survivor who just made the unhook: Leverage slows their healing for {{Leverage|reducehealingduration}} s.

builds.title: The Basement Build
builds.summary: Basement hooks become Scourge Hooks: Pain Resonance explodes the generator with the most progress on each Survivor's first Scourge Hook, and Monstrous Shrine speeds regression while you are away from the hook.
builds.details: Monstrous Shrine turns the basement hooks into Scourge Hooks alongside the random ones, and as long as you are at least {{Scourge Hook: Monstrous Shrine|range}} m from a Survivor on a Scourge Hook, Monstrous Shrine makes any generator that is not being repaired regress at {{Scourge Hook: Monstrous Shrine|generatorregression}}% speed. Pain Resonance starts with {{Scourge Hook: Pain Resonance|startingtokens}} Tokens and spends one the first time each Survivor is hooked on a Scourge Hook, making the generator with the most progress explode, lose {{Scourge Hook: Pain Resonance|generatorregression%}}% progress and start regressing, and Survivors repairing it scream. While carrying, Agitation gives you {{Agitation|haste%}}% Haste and a {{Agitation|terrorradiusincreasesize}} m larger Terror Radius, and Mad Grit removes the cooldown after a missed basic attack and stops the carried Survivor's wiggle progress for {{Mad Grit|wigglepauseduration}} s whenever your basic attack damages someone. Game Rant presents it as a niche pick for territorial killers.
tips: Monstrous Shrine only works while you are at least {{Scourge Hook: Monstrous Shrine|range}} m from the hooked Survivor, so standing guard at the basement switches its regression off.
Pain Resonance fires once per Survivor, on their first Scourge Hook (with Monstrous Shrine the basement hooks are Scourge Hooks), so spread your first Scourge hooks across different Survivors.
The Game Rant article dates from October 2024; the numbers shown here are the current live values.
Game Rant recommends area-denial killers such as The Trapper or The Huntress.

builds.title: Item Thief Wallhacks (Franklin's + Weave)
builds.summary: Franklin's Demise knocks items to the floor on basic-attack hits, and Weave Attunement shows you anyone within {{Weave Attunement|aurarevealdistance}} m of a dropped item, so lost items become bait.
builds.details: Franklin's Demise makes a Survivor drop their item whenever you damage them with a basic attack and shows you dropped items within {{Franklin's Demise|itemsrevealdistance}} m; Weave Attunement also drops each item the first time it is depleted. While a Survivor is within {{Weave Attunement|aurarevealdistance}} m of a dropped item you see their Aura (and they see the item's), and picking an item up makes them Oblivious for {{Weave Attunement|obliviousduration}} s. Hoarder adds {{Hoarder|extrachestsspawned}} chests at the start and alerts you whenever a Survivor within {{Hoarder|revealdistance}} m of you picks up an item or starts unlocking a chest. Human Greed lets you lock chests (cooldown {{Human Greed|cooldown}} s), shows you locked chests, and reveals a Survivor's Aura for {{Human Greed|aurarevealduration}} s when they come within {{Human Greed|aurarevealrange}} m of one.
tips: Franklin's Demise needs basic-attack damage; the video shows the build on The Unknown, The Executioner, The Slasher and The Huntress.
Lock chests near generators with Human Greed so Survivors who walk past them reveal themselves.
Hoarder's alert only covers item pick-ups and chest unlocking within {{Hoarder|revealdistance}} m of you.

builds.title: Exhaustion Shutdown
builds.summary: Hex: Under Your Thumb caps a running Survivor's Haste at {{Hex: Under Your Thumb|hastecap}}% and alerts you to speed boosts nearby, while Bamboozle blocks windows you vault and Batteries Included speeds you up near finished generators.
builds.details: Under Your Thumb lights its Dull Totem the first time any Survivor gains a Hook State; from then on, running Survivors cannot have more than {{Hex: Under Your Thumb|hastecap}}% Haste at a time, and you are alerted whenever a running Survivor gains Haste within {{Hex: Under Your Thumb|hasterange}} m of you. Undying lights at the start of the trial, and if Under Your Thumb is cleansed or blessed while Undying's totem still stands, the Hex moves onto Undying's totem. Bamboozle blocks each window you vault for Survivors for {{Bamboozle|windowblockdurations}} s (only one window at a time) and lets you basic-vault {{Bamboozle|windowvaultspeed%}}% faster, and Batteries Included gives you {{Batteries Included|haste%}}% Haste within {{Batteries Included|requireddistance}} m of a completed generator, lasting {{Batteries Included|hastelingerduration}} s after you leave. That is what makes it toxic: large speed boosts are capped and the window you just vaulted is closed to Survivors.
tips: The Hex only lights the first time a Survivor gains a Hook State, so secure an early hook.
Under Your Thumb's alert only covers running Survivors within {{Hex: Under Your Thumb|hasterange}} m of you, and it tells you a speed boost has just been used.
Vault the window a Survivor is looping to block it for {{Bamboozle|windowblockdurations}} s; only one window can be blocked at a time.
The video uses it on The Pig, The Cannibal, The Oni and The Unknown.

builds.title: Skill-Check Hell
builds.summary: Kicking a generator makes Overcharge and Oppression hand out special skill checks, while each hook gives Huntress Lullaby a Token that makes basic skill checks harder and finally removes their warning.
builds.details: Whenever you damage a generator, Overcharge ramps its regression from {{Overcharge|startingregressionspeed%}}% to {{Overcharge|maxregressionspeed%}}% speed over {{Overcharge|regressionrampduration}} s and gives the next Survivor who starts repairing it a special skill check that costs {{Overcharge|genregressiononfail%}}% extra progress if missed. On the same kick, Oppression (cooldown {{Oppression|cooldown}} s) makes up to {{Oppression|affectedgenerators}} other generators start regressing and gives Survivors repairing them a special skill check. Huntress Lullaby earns a Token per hook; each Token makes basic skill check warnings appear later and good zones smaller, at {{Hex: Huntress Lullaby|maxtokens}} Tokens the warnings stop appearing, and every missed basic skill check costs {{Hex: Huntress Lullaby|regressionbonus%}}% more progress. If Lullaby's totem is cleansed or blessed while Undying's still stands, Lullaby moves onto Undying's totem and keeps its Tokens.
tips: Overcharge's special skill check goes to the next Survivor who starts repairing the generator you kicked; Oppression's go to Survivors on the other generators it made regress.
Huntress Lullaby only changes basic skill checks, so it does not affect the special checks from Overcharge and Oppression.
Hook early and often: Lullaby's warnings only disappear once it has {{Hex: Huntress Lullaby|maxtokens}} Tokens.
Demonstrated on The Nemesis, The Doctor, The Blight and The Skull Merchant.

builds.title: Oblivious + Blindness Slasher
builds.summary: Third Seal gives Blindness to Survivors you damage, Plaything makes Survivors Oblivious from their first hook, and Deathbound makes a Survivor who heals a teammate scream and stay Oblivious while away from them.
builds.details: Third Seal lights a totem at the start and gives Blindness to Survivors you damage with a basic or special attack, up to {{Hex: The Third Seal|maxaffectedsurvivors}} of them. The first time you hook each Survivor, Plaything hexes them and lights a totem that is blocked for other Survivors for {{Hex: Plaything|totemblockduration}} s; the hexed Survivor is Oblivious and sees that totem's Aura within {{Hex: Plaything|totemaurarevealdistance}} m. When a Survivor finishes healing another, Deathbound makes the healer scream, then keeps them Oblivious, and shows them the healed Survivor's Aura, while they are at least {{Deathbound|maximumdistance}} m apart, until the healer takes damage (one Survivor at a time). Thanatophobia slows repairs, totem cleansing and hook sabotage by {{Thanatophobia|actionspeedpenaltypersurvivor%}}% per injured, downed or hooked Survivor, plus {{Thanatophobia|actionspeedpenaltybonus%}}% once all four are.
tips: Paired in the video with the Party Noisemaker and Toxic Waste add-ons.
Third Seal and Plaything both need totems, so Plaything stops lighting once no Dull Totems are left.
Deathbound works on one healer at a time and ends when that healer takes damage.
The creator lists this among the five nastiest killer setups of 2026.

builds.title: Head Pop Pig
builds.summary: Three scream perks keep showing you where Survivors are: THWACK! on pallet and wall breaks, Face the Darkness on a timer while the Survivor you damaged stays injured, and Phantom Fear when someone looks at you.
builds.details: THWACK! starts with {{THWACK!|startingtokens}} Tokens (up to {{THWACK!|maxtokens}}) and earns one per hook; each pallet or breakable wall you break while you have a Token spends one, making all Survivors within {{THWACK!|range}} m scream and showing you their Auras for {{THWACK!|revealduration}} s. Damaging a Survivor hexes them and lights Face the Darkness, and from then on every {{Hex: Face the Darkness|screaminterval}} s the other Survivors outside your Terror Radius scream and you see their Auras for {{Hex: Face the Darkness|aurarevealduration}} s; the totem goes out when the hexed Survivor is downed or becomes healthy. Phantom Fear makes a Survivor inside your Terror Radius scream and reveals their Aura for {{Phantom Fear|aurarevealduration}} s when they look at you (cooldown {{Phantom Fear|cooldown}} s), and Ruin makes every generator nobody is repairing regress at {{Hex: Ruin|regressionspeed%}}% speed while you go looking. The video runs it on The Pig.
tips: THWACK! spends a Token automatically on every break while it has one, so the screams happen on whichever pallets and walls you break first; each hook gives a Token back (up to {{THWACK!|maxtokens}}).
Face the Darkness only runs while the Survivor you damaged stays injured, so downing them ends it.
Video add-ons: Tampered Timer and Crate of Gears.

builds.title: Ultimate Snowball Blight
builds.summary: Infectious Fright makes Survivors in your Terror Radius scream whenever someone is downed, and Forced Hesitation (with a cooldown) Hinders Survivors near the body, so you can leave the downed Survivor and chase the next one.
builds.details: Whenever a Survivor is downed, Infectious Fright makes Survivors within your Terror Radius scream and alerts you for {{Infectious Fright|revealduration}} s. When you down a Survivor, Forced Hesitation gives other Survivors within {{Forced Hesitation|requireddistance}} m of them {{Forced Hesitation|hinder%}}% Hindered for {{Forced Hesitation|hinderedduration}} s (cooldown {{Forced Hesitation|cooldown}} s). Blood Favor blocks upright pallets within {{Hex: Blood Favor|effectradius}} m of a healthy Survivor for {{Hex: Blood Favor|blockduration}} s when your basic attack injures them, and if Blood Favor's totem is cleansed or blessed while Undying's still stands, Blood Favor moves onto Undying's totem.
tips: Only pick up when nobody else is close; the build is about leaving Survivors on the ground to keep momentum.
Blood Favor only triggers when a basic attack takes a healthy Survivor to injured, not on downs.
Forced Hesitation has a {{Forced Hesitation|cooldown}} s cooldown, so of two quick downs only the first Hinders Survivors within {{Forced Hesitation|requireddistance}} m.

builds.title: Exposed Deathslinger
builds.summary: Three ways to make Survivors Exposed: Make your Choice on unhooks while you are far away, Dragon's Grip on the first repair of a generator you kicked, and Devour Hope once it has enough Tokens.
builds.details: Make your Choice makes a Survivor who unhooks another or themselves scream and become Exposed for {{Make your Choice|exposedduration}} s if you are at least {{Make your Choice|minimumdistance}} m away at the time (cooldown {{Make your Choice|cooldown}} s). Whenever you damage a generator, Dragon's Grip waits {{Dragon’s Grip|activeduration}} s for the first Survivor to repair it; that Survivor screams, you are alerted to their position for {{Dragon’s Grip|aurarevealduration}} s and they become Exposed for {{Dragon’s Grip|exposedduration}} s (cooldown {{Dragon’s Grip|cooldown}} s). Devour Hope earns a Token for each unhook that happens while you are at least {{Hex: Devour Hope|distancefromhook}} m away: at {{Hex: Devour Hope|tokensforexposed}} Tokens all Survivors are Exposed and at {{Hex: Devour Hope|tokensformori}} Tokens you can kill downed Survivors. If Devour Hope's totem is cleansed or blessed while Undying's still stands, the Hex moves onto Undying's totem and keeps its Tokens.
tips: After a hook, walk at least {{Make your Choice|minimumdistance}} m away: that is far enough for both Make your Choice and Devour Hope's {{Hex: Devour Hope|distancefromhook}} m.
Dragon's Grip only affects the first Survivor to repair that generator within {{Dragon’s Grip|activeduration}} s of your kick.
Until Devour Hope reaches {{Hex: Devour Hope|tokensforexposed}} Tokens, your Exposed comes from Make your Choice and Dragon's Grip.

builds.title: Anti-Turret Xenomorph
builds.summary: A basic-attack build: Save the best for last shortens your attack cooldown as you hit non-Obsession Survivors, Blood Favor blocks pallets around fresh injuries and Celestial Witness moves or reveals the Obsession.
builds.details: Save the best for last earns a Token (up to {{Save the best for last|maxtokens}}) whenever you damage a Survivor who is not the Obsession with a basic attack, and each Token makes your successful basic-attack cooldown {{Save the best for last|attackreductionpertoken%}}% shorter; damage to the Obsession removes {{Save the best for last|tokenslostonhit}} Tokens, and none can be earned while the Obsession is dead. Every {{Celestial Witness|timer}} s, Celestial Witness shows you the Obsession's Aura for {{Celestial Witness|auraduration}} s if they are at least {{Celestial Witness|distance}} m away; otherwise the farthest Survivor becomes the Obsession, so an Obsession you are chasing up close usually passes the role to someone farther away. Blood Favor blocks upright pallets within {{Hex: Blood Favor|effectradius}} m of a healthy Survivor for {{Hex: Blood Favor|blockduration}} s when your basic attack injures them, and Batteries Included gives you {{Batteries Included|haste%}}% Haste within {{Batteries Included|requireddistance}} m of a completed generator.
tips: Avoid damaging the Obsession: each time they take damage you lose {{Save the best for last|tokenslostonhit}} Save the best for last Tokens.

If you are chasing the Obsession within {{Celestial Witness|distance}} m at a check, Celestial Witness makes the farthest Survivor the Obsession instead, so your hits on the one you are chasing can then earn Save the best for last Tokens.
The creator ranks it among the most oppressive killer setups of 2026.
Video add-ons: Cat Carrier and Harpoon Gun.

builds.title: Slugging Twins
builds.summary: A slugging setup for The Twins: downs make Survivors in your Terror Radius scream and Hinder those near the body (with a cooldown), and Third Seal gives Blindness to up to {{Hex: The Third Seal|maxaffectedsurvivors}} Survivors you damage.
builds.details: Whenever a Survivor is downed, Infectious Fright makes Survivors within your Terror Radius scream and alerts you for {{Infectious Fright|revealduration}} s, and when you down someone, Forced Hesitation gives other Survivors within {{Forced Hesitation|requireddistance}} m of them {{Forced Hesitation|hinder%}}% Hindered for {{Forced Hesitation|hinderedduration}} s (cooldown {{Forced Hesitation|cooldown}} s). Third Seal lights a totem at the start of the trial and gives Blindness to Survivors you damage with a basic or special attack, up to {{Hex: The Third Seal|maxaffectedsurvivors}} of them. Undying also lights at the start; if Third Seal's totem is cleansed or blessed while Undying's still stands, Third Seal moves onto Undying's totem.
tips: From a video about making forgotten killers oppressive; add-ons used there: Forest Stew and Madeleine’s Scarf.
Forced Hesitation only Hinders Survivors who are already within {{Forced Hesitation|requireddistance}} m when the down happens, not someone who arrives later.

builds.title: Slugging Krasue
builds.summary: Distressing enlarges your Terror Radius, and Infectious Fright makes everyone inside it scream whenever someone goes down, so you can leave a Survivor on the ground and go after the next one.
builds.details: Distressing makes your Terror Radius larger and slows repairs inside it by {{Distressing|repairspeedpenalty}}%, and Infectious Fright makes every Survivor inside that radius scream when anyone is downed, alerting you for {{Infectious Fright|revealduration}} s. Ruin makes every generator that is not being repaired regress at {{Hex: Ruin|regressionspeed%}}% speed, so Survivors who leave their generator to help a teammate lose progress. If the match reaches the gates, Blood Warden blocks both exits for {{Blood Warden|gateblockduration}} s the first time you hook someone after an Exit Gate has opened (once per trial) and shows you Survivors inside the exit thresholds.
tips: Smaller-creator source; the perk list is given verbatim in the video description.
Infectious Fright only reaches Survivors inside your Terror Radius, so Distressing's larger radius directly widens what you hear.
Blood Warden works once per trial and needs a hook after an Exit Gate has been opened.

builds.title: Snowball Executioner
builds.summary: A Nurse's Calling shows you Survivors who are healing and Coulrophobia slows heals inside your Terror Radius, while Infectious Fright and Forced Hesitation (with a cooldown) make nearby Survivors scream and become Hindered after a down.
builds.details: A Nurse's Calling shows you the Auras of Survivors within {{A Nurse's Calling|aurarevealdistance}} m who are healing or being healed, and Coulrophobia makes Survivors in your Terror Radius heal {{Coulrophobia|healpenalty%}}% slower with basic skill checks spinning {{Coulrophobia|skillcheckspeedincrease%}}% faster while they heal. Whenever a Survivor is downed, Infectious Fright makes Survivors within your Terror Radius scream and alerts you for {{Infectious Fright|revealduration}} s. When you down a Survivor, Forced Hesitation also gives other Survivors within {{Forced Hesitation|requireddistance}} m of them {{Forced Hesitation|hinder%}}% Hindered for {{Forced Hesitation|hinderedduration}} s (cooldown {{Forced Hesitation|cooldown}} s), which helps you reach the next target instead of carrying.
tips: Coulrophobia only slows heals inside your Terror Radius; The Executioner's base Terror Radius matches A Nurse's Calling's {{A Nurse's Calling|aurarevealdistance}} m, so healing Survivors it shows you are normally inside it too.
Video add-ons: Leopard-Print Fabric and Misty Day, Rites of Judgment.

builds.title: Impossible Skill Checks Doctor
builds.summary: Smaller good zones, faster healing checks and, after enough hooks, no warning at all: a skill-check build for The Doctor built on a larger Terror Radius and Huntress Lullaby.
builds.details: Distressing makes your Terror Radius {{Distressing|terrorradiusincreasesize}}% larger and slows repairs inside it by {{Distressing|repairspeedpenalty}}%. Inside the radius, Unnerving Presence gives Survivors {{Unnerving Presence|skillcheckoddsincrease%}}% more basic skill checks (and its text makes the good zone of basic skill checks {{Unnerving Presence|successzonesizepenalty%}}% smaller), and Coulrophobia makes them heal {{Coulrophobia|healpenalty%}}% slower with basic skill checks spinning {{Coulrophobia|skillcheckspeedincrease%}}% faster while healing. Huntress Lullaby is not tied to your Terror Radius: each hook earns a Token that makes basic skill check warnings appear later and good zones smaller, at {{Hex: Huntress Lullaby|maxtokens}} Tokens the warnings stop appearing, and every missed basic skill check costs {{Hex: Huntress Lullaby|regressionbonus%}}% more progress.
tips: Older source (July 2025); the perk names are unchanged and the numbers shown here are the current live values.
Unnerving Presence and Huntress Lullaby both shrink good zones, and same-kind skill-check modifiers are subject to Diminishing Returns, so the two may not add up in full.
Lullaby is the only Hex here and has no backup, so start hooking early.

builds.title: Walking Terror Radius Legion
builds.summary: Damage the Obsession and Dark Devotion hands them your Terror Radius while you stay Undetectable, the idea being that Coulrophobia's slower healing and Distressing's slower repairs then hit Survivors near them.
builds.details: Whenever the Obsession takes damage, Dark Devotion sets your Terror Radius to {{Dark Devotion|terrorradiussize}} m for {{Dark Devotion|terrorradiustransferduration}} s, gives that Terror Radius to the Obsession and makes you Undetectable. Coulrophobia makes Survivors within your Terror Radius heal {{Coulrophobia|healpenalty%}}% slower with basic skill checks spinning {{Coulrophobia|skillcheckspeedincrease%}}% faster while they heal, and Distressing slows their repairs by {{Distressing|repairspeedpenalty}}%; the idea is that while Dark Devotion is active, Survivors near the Obsession, who carries your Terror Radius, are the ones caught by both. Whenever you hook a Survivor, Blood Echo gives every injured Survivor Exhausted and Haemorrhage for {{Blood Echo|hemorrhageexhaustionduration}} s.
tips: Each time the Obsession takes damage, Dark Devotion triggers again for {{Dark Devotion|terrorradiustransferduration}} s.
Exhausted stops a Survivor's Exhaustion perks from triggering, so Blood Echo shuts them off for injured Survivors for {{Blood Echo|hemorrhageexhaustionduration}} s after each hook.
How Distressing's larger radius combines with Dark Devotion's fixed {{Dark Devotion|terrorradiussize}} m is not documented.

builds.title: Fuming Mixtape Hex Legion
builds.summary: Four Hexes: Ruin regresses idle generators, Face the Darkness makes distant Survivors scream while your target stays injured, Thrill of the Hunt blocks your totems on hooks and Undying backs up the first other Hex cleansed.
builds.details: Ruin makes every generator that is not being repaired regress at {{Hex: Ruin|regressionspeed%}}% speed, and Undying is also lit at the start: the first other Hex that is cleansed or blessed moves onto Undying's totem, so the backup may go to Face the Darkness or Thrill of the Hunt rather than Ruin. Whenever you damage a Survivor, Face the Darkness hexes them and lights a Dull Totem; from then on every {{Hex: Face the Darkness|screaminterval}} s the other Survivors outside your Terror Radius scream and you see their Auras for {{Hex: Face the Darkness|aurarevealduration}} s. That totem goes out when the hexed Survivor is downed or becomes healthy. Thrill of the Hunt lights on your first hook, and each hook then blocks all Hex Totems for {{Hex: Thrill of the Hunt|blockdurationpertoken}} s for each lit Hex Totem; the name comes from the Fuming Mix Tape add-on used in the video.
tips: Rotate between injured Survivors rather than committing: downing the Survivor hexed by Face the Darkness puts its totem out.
Every Hex needs its own totem, so Face the Darkness can only light while a Dull Totem is left.
Thrill of the Hunt blocks totems for longer the more Hexes are lit, so it is strongest while all four stand.

builds.title: Basement Trapper
builds.summary: Every basement hook is a Scourge Hook for Monstrous Shrine, so staying away speeds up regression, and a rescue made while you are far away leaves the rescuer Exposed through Make your Choice.
builds.details: Monstrous Shrine makes the basement hooks Scourge Hooks, and while you are at least {{Scourge Hook: Monstrous Shrine|range}} m from a Survivor on a Scourge Hook, every generator that is not being repaired regresses at {{Scourge Hook: Monstrous Shrine|generatorregression}}% speed. If a Survivor is unhooked while you are at least {{Make your Choice|minimumdistance}} m away, Make your Choice makes the one who unhooked scream and become Exposed for {{Make your Choice|exposedduration}} s (cooldown {{Make your Choice|cooldown}} s). Agitation gives you {{Agitation|haste%}}% Haste and a {{Agitation|terrorradiusincreasesize}} m larger Terror Radius while carrying, which helps you reach the basement. Crowd Control lights a totem the first time a Survivor medium- or fast-vaults a window, then blocks the last {{Hex: Crowd Control|maximumvaultsblocked}} windows Survivors medium- or fast-vaulted and shows you blocked windows within {{Hex: Crowd Control|aurarevealdistance}} m.
tips: Stay at least {{Make your Choice|minimumdistance}} m from the basement after a hook: that keeps both Make your Choice and Monstrous Shrine ({{Scourge Hook: Monstrous Shrine|range}} m) working.
The video runs it on The Trapper, hooking in the basement before walking away.
From a November 2026 video about making the basement as hard to leave as possible.

builds.title: Basement Hag
builds.summary: Hook in the basement and leave: Monstrous Shrine regresses generators while you are away, Make your Choice exposes the Survivor who unhooks while you are far off, and Save the best for last shortens your basic-attack cooldown.
builds.details: Monstrous Shrine turns the basement hooks into Scourge Hooks, and while you are at least {{Scourge Hook: Monstrous Shrine|range}} m from a Survivor on a Scourge Hook every generator that is not being repaired regresses at {{Scourge Hook: Monstrous Shrine|generatorregression}}% speed. If someone unhooks a Survivor, or unhooks themselves, while you are at least {{Make your Choice|minimumdistance}} m away, Make your Choice makes the one who unhooked scream and become Exposed for {{Make your Choice|exposedduration}} s (cooldown {{Make your Choice|cooldown}} s). Save the best for last earns a Token (up to {{Save the best for last|maxtokens}}) each time your basic attack damages a Survivor who is not the Obsession, and each Token makes your successful basic-attack cooldown {{Save the best for last|attackreductionpertoken%}}% shorter, while Agitation gives you {{Agitation|haste%}}% Haste and a {{Agitation|terrorradiusincreasesize}} m larger Terror Radius as you carry.
tips: Each time the Obsession takes damage you lose {{Save the best for last|tokenslostonhit}} Save the best for last Tokens, so leave them for last.

Leave after hooking: Monstrous Shrine needs you at least {{Scourge Hook: Monstrous Shrine|range}} m from the hooked Survivor and Make your Choice needs {{Make your Choice|minimumdistance}} m at the moment of the unhook.
The video runs it on The Hag, hooking in the basement and then leaving.

builds.title: Basement Demogorgon
builds.summary: Carry Survivors to the basement with Agitation's Haste and Iron Grasp's slower wiggle, then leave: Territorial Imperative shows who walks in and Make your Choice exposes the Survivor who unhooks while you are far away.
builds.details: While you carry a Survivor, Agitation gives you {{Agitation|haste%}}% Haste and a {{Agitation|terrorradiusincreasesize}} m larger Terror Radius, and Iron Grasp makes their wiggle {{Iron Grasp|wiggletimeincrease%}}% slower and {{Iron Grasp|wigglestrengthreduction%}}% weaker, which helps you reach the basement. Territorial Imperative shows you the Aura of a Survivor who enters the basement for {{Territorial Imperative|revealtime}} s while you are {{Territorial Imperative|minimumdistance}} m or more away from it (cooldown {{Territorial Imperative|cooldown}} s), your cue to head back. If a Survivor is unhooked while you are at least {{Make your Choice|minimumdistance}} m away, Make your Choice makes the one who unhooked scream and become Exposed for {{Make your Choice|exposedduration}} s (cooldown {{Make your Choice|cooldown}} s).
tips: When Territorial Imperative shows someone entering the basement, head back, but stay at least {{Make your Choice|minimumdistance}} m away until the unhook happens if you want Make your Choice to trigger.
Territorial Imperative has a {{Territorial Imperative|cooldown}} s cooldown, so a second Survivor entering right after the first may not show up.

builds.title: Anti-Heal Mastermind
builds.summary: A bigger terror radius where healing is slower, skill checks spin faster and healers turn Blind and Exhausted, while A Nurse's Calling shows nearby heals.
builds.details: Distressing makes The Mastermind's terror radius {{Distressing|terrorradiusincreasesize}}% larger and slows repairs inside it by {{Distressing|repairspeedpenalty}}%, and Coulrophobia makes survivors inside it heal {{Coulrophobia|healpenalty%}}% slower while their basic skill checks spin {{Coulrophobia|skillcheckspeedincrease%}}% faster as they heal. Septic Touch gives anyone healing inside your terror radius Blindness and Exhausted, which last until {{Septic Touch|blindnessexhaustionduration}} s after they stop healing. A Nurse's Calling shows you the auras of survivors healing or being healed within {{A Nurse's Calling|aurarevealdistance}} m, so you know which heal to interrupt.
tips: Coulrophobia, Septic Touch and Distressing's repair penalty only reach survivors inside your terror radius; A Nurse's Calling works within {{A Nurse's Calling|aurarevealdistance}} m of you instead.
Septic Touch's Exhausted keeps a healer's Exhaustion perks from triggering until it wears off, and its Blindness stops them reading auras.
A Nurse's Calling shows both the survivor healing and the one being healed.

builds.title: Anti-Heal Clown
builds.summary: Coulrophobia on its original owner, with Scourge Hook rescues and Thanatophobia making every injury cost the team time.
builds.details: Distressing makes The Clown's terror radius {{Distressing|terrorradiusincreasesize}}% larger, widening the area where Coulrophobia makes survivors heal {{Coulrophobia|healpenalty%}}% slower and Distressing slows repairs by {{Distressing|repairspeedpenalty}}%. A survivor unhooked from one of the 4 Scourge Hooks gets Haemorrhage and Mangled for {{Scourge Hook: Gift of Pain|mangledhemorrhageduration}} s from Gift of Pain, and once healed they heal and repair {{Scourge Hook: Gift of Pain|actionspeeddebuff%}}% slower until they next take damage. Thanatophobia slows every survivor's repairs, totem cleansing and hook sabotage by {{Thanatophobia|actionspeedpenaltypersurvivor%}}% for each injured, downed or hooked survivor, plus another {{Thanatophobia|actionspeedpenaltybonus%}}% while all 4 are.
tips: Hook on Scourge Hooks when you can: Gift of Pain only triggers when someone is unhooked from one.
Thanatophobia counts downed and hooked survivors as well as injured ones.
Gift of Pain's slower healing and repairing ends when that survivor takes damage, so it lasts longest on survivors you leave alone after they heal.

builds.title: Anti-Heal Nurse
builds.summary: Slow heals inside the terror radius, screams outside it, and Exhausted plus Haemorrhage for the injured after every hook.
builds.details: Distressing makes the terror radius {{Distressing|terrorradiusincreasesize}}% larger and Coulrophobia makes survivors inside it heal {{Coulrophobia|healpenalty%}}% slower, with basic skill checks spinning faster while they heal. Damaging a survivor hexes them and lights Face the Darkness on a Dull Totem: every {{Hex: Face the Darkness|screaminterval}} s the other survivors outside your terror radius scream and you see their auras for {{Hex: Face the Darkness|aurarevealduration}} s. The hex lasts until that survivor is healthy again or in the dying state. Whenever you hook someone, Blood Echo gives all injured survivors Exhausted and Haemorrhage for {{Blood Echo|hemorrhageexhaustionduration}} s.
tips: Face the Darkness needs a Dull Totem left when you hit someone, and its totem goes out once the hexed survivor is downed or healed.
Distressing and Face the Darkness pull against each other: the bigger the terror radius, the fewer survivors are outside it to scream.
Blood Echo's Exhausted keeps injured survivors from using Exhaustion perks while it lasts.

builds.title: Status-Effect Huntress
builds.summary: Blindness, Oblivious, Broken and Exposed from four perks, each with its own trigger.
builds.details: The Third Seal gives Blindness to up to {{Hex: The Third Seal|maxaffectedsurvivors}} survivors you damage with a basic or special attack, and Plaything makes each survivor Oblivious after their first hook, with that Hex Totem blocked to the others for {{Hex: Plaything|totemblockduration}} s. No Quarter gives self-healers special skill checks at {{No Quarter|selfhealtrigger%}}% progress and makes them Broken for {{No Quarter|brokenduration}} s if they miss one or stop healing. Iron Maiden makes anyone leaving a locker Exposed for {{Iron Maiden|exposedduration}} s and lets you open lockers {{Iron Maiden|actionspeed%}}% faster; the video is about stacking as many status effects as possible.
tips: Blindness stops survivors reading auras and Oblivious stops them perceiving your terror radius, so affected survivors get much less warning.
Plaything's hexed survivor sees its totem's aura within {{Hex: Plaything|totemaurarevealdistance}} m, so expect them to go for it once the block ends.
Iron Maiden also makes a survivor leaving a locker scream and alerts you to their location for {{Iron Maiden|revealduration}} s.
The video also runs the Begrimed Head and Venomous Concoction add-ons.

builds.title: Starstruck Ghost Face
builds.summary: Pick someone up and every survivor inside the terror radius becomes Exposed, with faster pick-ups and drops to punish rescuers.
builds.details: While Ghost Face carries a survivor, Starstruck makes everyone inside his terror radius Exposed until {{Starstruck|exposedlingerduration}} s after they leave it or he drops or hooks the carried survivor; it has a {{Starstruck|cooldown}} s cooldown. Distressing enlarges that terror radius, so more of the rescue party is caught. Forever Entwined (a Token whenever a survivor takes damage, up to {{Forever Entwined|maxtokens}}) and Fire Up (a Token per completed generator, up to {{Fire Up|maxtokens}}) both speed up pick-ups and drops, so dropping the carried survivor to hit an Exposed rescuer and picking up again costs less time.
tips: Older source (November 2025).
Starstruck's Exposed keeps running for {{Starstruck|exposedlingerduration}} s after you drop the survivor, so a drop to go after a rescuer does not end it straight away.
Forever Entwined also makes you hook survivors {{Forever Entwined|bonuspertoken%}}% faster per Token.

builds.title: Hex Chase Freddy
builds.summary: Four hexes that block pallets and windows and slow down survivors who take basic-attack hits.
builds.details: Blood Favor blocks upright pallets within {{Hex: Blood Favor|effectradius}} m of a healthy survivor you injure with a basic attack for {{Hex: Blood Favor|blockduration}} s, and Crowd Control keeps the last {{Hex: Crowd Control|maximumvaultsblocked}} windows that survivors medium- or fast-vaulted blocked. Once you have damaged survivors with {{Hex: Nothing But Misery|basichitsrequired}} basic attacks, Nothing But Misery lights; from then on every basic-attack hit gives {{Hex: Nothing But Misery|hindered%}}% Hindered for {{Hex: Nothing But Misery|hinderedduration}} s, and makes the survivor {{Hex: Nothing But Misery|vault%}}% slower at vaulting for {{Hex: Nothing But Misery|vaultduration}} s. Undying protects whichever other hex is cleansed or blessed first by moving it onto Undying's own totem.
tips: Crowd Control and Nothing But Misery light their totems later, so they need a Dull Totem left at that moment.
Undying shows you survivors within {{Hex: Undying|aurarevealdistance}} m of Dull Totems, which helps you protect the spare totems those two hexes need.
You basic-vault Crowd Control's blocked windows {{Hex: Crowd Control|vaultspeedincrease%}}% faster and see their auras within {{Hex: Crowd Control|aurarevealdistance}} m.

builds.title: Hex Devour Dredge
builds.summary: Stay away from your hooks to grow Devour Hope's Tokens, while Thrill of the Hunt, Undying and Pentimento make removing the totems costly.
builds.details: Devour Hope earns a Token whenever a survivor is unhooked while you are at least {{Hex: Devour Hope|distancefromhook}} m away: at {{Hex: Devour Hope|tokensforhaste}} Tokens you gain {{Hex: Devour Hope|haste%}}% Haste {{Hex: Devour Hope|hastedelayduration}} s after each hook, at {{Hex: Devour Hope|tokensforexposed}} survivors are Exposed, and at {{Hex: Devour Hope|tokensformori}} you can kill downed survivors. Thrill of the Hunt lights at your first hook, and each hook blocks all Hex Totems for {{Hex: Thrill of the Hunt|blockdurationpertoken}} s per lit Hex Totem; Undying moves the first other hex to be cleansed or blessed onto its own totem, Tokens included. Pentimento shows you cleansed totems and lets you rekindle each once, and while at least one rekindled totem stands, survivors heal and repair {{Hex: Pentimento|baseactionspeedpenalty%}}% slower, plus {{Hex: Pentimento|actionspeedpenaltypertotem%}}% for each extra rekindled totem.
tips: Devour Hope only counts unhooks that happen while you are at least {{Hex: Devour Hope|distancefromhook}} m away, so leave the hook area after hooking.
Thrill of the Hunt needs a Dull Totem left when you first hook, and its block gets shorter as fewer hexes stay lit.
Pentimento works on any cleansed totem, so survivors cleansing dull totems also give you something to rekindle.

builds.title: Hex Stealth Oni
builds.summary: Oblivious and Blindness take away survivors' terror-radius warning and aura reading, and Overture of Doom sometimes moves your terror radius onto a generator.
builds.details: Plaything makes each survivor Oblivious after their first hook, and Retribution makes anyone who starts blessing or cleansing a totem Oblivious for {{Hex: Retribution|obliviousduration}} s, so they cannot perceive your terror radius. The Third Seal gives Blindness, which stops aura reading, to up to {{Hex: The Third Seal|maxaffectedsurvivors}} survivors you damage with a basic or special attack. Overture of Doom hexes the generator farthest from its totem: after a survivor repairs it for {{Hex: Overture of Doom|requiredtime}} s, you become Undetectable and your terror radius sits on that generator for {{Hex: Overture of Doom|terrorradiusdisplacementduration}} s.
tips: If survivors cleanse or bless a Hex Totem, Retribution shows you every survivor's aura for {{Hex: Retribution|aurarevealduration}} s.
Plaything lights later, so it needs a Dull Totem left after the three hexes that start lit.
When the hexed generator is repaired, Overture of Doom moves to the next farthest one.

builds.title: Endgame Mori Singularity
builds.summary: Locate every survivor on each generator completion, then kill the Exposed Obsession once the last one is done.
builds.details: Whenever a generator is completed, Rancor alerts you to every survivor's position for {{Rancor|survivorrevealduration}} s, and once all are done it makes the Obsession Exposed and lets you kill them. Game Afoot gives {{Game Afoot|haste%}}% Haste for {{Game Afoot|hasteduration}} s when you break a pallet or wall or damage a generator while chasing the Obsession. Remember Me earns a Token each time the Obsession takes damage (up to {{Remember Me|maximumtokens}}) and makes everyone else open exit gates {{Remember Me|actionspeedpenalty%}}% slower per Token, while Terminus makes every injured, downed or hooked survivor Broken when the last generator is completed, ending {{Terminus|brokenduration}} s after a gate opens.
tips: Game Afoot makes the survivor with the most chase time the Obsession when you hit them with a basic attack, which also changes who Rancor and Remember Me target.
Each generator completion also shows your aura to the Obsession for {{Rancor|killerrevealduration}} s.
Source is from December 2025.

builds.title: Unopenable Gates Springtrap
builds.summary: Slow gate switches, punish anyone who lets go of one late, and block the exits after a hook once a gate is open.
builds.details: Remember Me makes survivors other than the Obsession open exit gates {{Remember Me|actionspeedpenalty%}}% slower for each Token, earned whenever the Obsession takes damage (up to {{Remember Me|maximumtokens}}). With Haywire, a switch with at least {{Haywire|regressionthreshold%}}% progress regresses at {{Haywire|regressionrate%}}% speed, so chasing a survivor off it late undoes progress. Terminus makes every injured, downed or hooked survivor Broken when the last generator is completed, lasting until {{Terminus|brokenduration}} s after a gate opens, and Blood Warden blocks both exits for {{Blood Warden|gateblockduration}} s on your first hook after a gate is opened (once per trial).
tips: Older source (July 2025).
Damage the Obsession {{Remember Me|maximumtokens}} times during the match for full Remember Me value.
Survivors see the gate lights flicker while Haywire regresses a switch, so they know it is happening.
The video plays it on The Animatronic with the Loot Bag add-on.

builds.title: Secret Project Gen-Lock Trapper
builds.summary: Corrupt Intervention, Deadlock and Dead Man's Switch keep blocking generators, and Secret Project makes Trapper Undetectable whenever any are blocked.
builds.details: Corrupt Intervention blocks the {{Corrupt Intervention|generatorsblocked}} generators farthest from you at the start for {{Corrupt Intervention|generatorblockduration}} s, or until you down a survivor. Deadlock blocks the most-progressed generator for {{Deadlock|generatorblockduration}} s whenever one is completed, and after each hook Dead Man’s Switch blocks the next generator a survivor stops repairing for more than {{Dead Man’s Switch|generatorreleaseduration}} s, for {{Dead Man’s Switch|generatorblockduration}} s ({{Dead Man’s Switch|cooldown}} s cooldown). Secret Project gives you Undetectable for {{Secret Project|undetectableduration}} s whenever one or more generators are blocked, and blocks a random unblocked generator for {{Secret Project|blockduration}} s each time a totem is blessed or cleansed.
tips: Use the time the blocks buy to set up around the generators that are still open.
Corrupt Intervention ends at your first down, so an early down trades it away.
Dead Man’s Switch blocks only the next generator a survivor leaves after a hook, not every one.

builds.title: Camp Crystal Lake Lockdown (Slasher endgame)
builds.summary: When the last generator finishes The Slasher turns Undetectable, while No Way Out and Remember Me keep the gates from opening quickly.
builds.details: No Way Out earns a Token the first time you hook each survivor; once all generators are done, a survivor who starts opening a gate finds it blocked for {{No Way Out|gateblockbaseduration}} s plus {{No Way Out|gateblockdurationpertoken}} s per Token, and you are alerted. Remember Me makes survivors other than the Obsession open gates {{Remember Me|actionspeedpenalty%}}% slower per Token (earned when the Obsession takes damage), and Silent Shadow makes you Undetectable when the last generator is completed, as well as for {{Silent Shadow|starttrialundetectableduration}} s after every hook. If a gate still opens, Blood Warden blocks both exits for {{Blood Warden|gateblockduration}} s on your next hook, once per trial.
tips: No Way Out's Tokens come only from the first hook on each survivor, so spread your hooks.
Blood Warden shows you the auras of survivors standing in the exit thresholds.
Video add-ons: Iridescent Boat Motor and Burnt Fuse.

builds.title: Chainsaw Snowball Bubba
builds.summary: Downs make survivors in your terror radius scream and, off cooldown, Hinder those near the body, so one down can lead to the next.
builds.details: Infectious Fright makes survivors inside your terror radius scream whenever someone is downed, alerting you to them for {{Infectious Fright|revealduration}} s, and Forced Hesitation gives the other survivors within {{Forced Hesitation|requireddistance}} m of the downed survivor {{Forced Hesitation|hinder%}}% Hindered for {{Forced Hesitation|hinderedduration}} s ({{Forced Hesitation|cooldown}} s cooldown). Corrupt Intervention blocks the {{Corrupt Intervention|generatorsblocked}} generators farthest from you for {{Corrupt Intervention|generatorblockduration}} s or until your first down, and Bamboozle blocks each window you vault for survivors for {{Bamboozle|windowblockdurations}} s. On The Cannibal the aim is to turn one down into the next before survivors can spread out.
tips: Older source (July 2025).
Infectious Fright triggers on any down, but Forced Hesitation only on downs you cause and only once per cooldown.
Bamboozle can only block one window at a time, and you basic-vault windows {{Bamboozle|windowvaultspeed%}}% faster.

builds.title: Blind and Oblivious Springtrap
builds.summary: Oblivious hooked survivors, Blind damaged ones, and a killer who goes Undetectable after damaging generators or hooking the Obsession.
builds.details: Plaything makes each survivor Oblivious after their first hook, so they cannot perceive your terror radius, and The Third Seal gives Blindness, which blocks aura reading, to up to {{Hex: The Third Seal|maxaffectedsurvivors}} survivors you damage. Whenever you damage a generator, Unforeseen makes you Undetectable and moves your terror radius to that generator with a radius of {{Unforeseen|terrorradiussize}} m for {{Unforeseen|effectduration}} s ({{Unforeseen|cooldown}} s cooldown). Furtive Chase gives {{Furtive Chase|haste%}}% Haste and Undetectable for {{Furtive Chase|undetectablehasteduration}} s each time you hook the Obsession, and the survivor who unhooks them becomes the new Obsession.
tips: Older source (July 2025).
Unforeseen only triggers when you damage a generator, so kicking one is how you go Undetectable between hooks.
Plaything lights a Dull Totem when it triggers, so it needs one left after The Third Seal's.

builds.title: Hit-and-Run Anti-Heal Wraith
builds.summary: Hit, leave, and come back when A Nurse's Calling shows a nearby heal, while Thanatophobia slows everyone for each injured survivor.
builds.details: Each basic-attack hit gives the survivor Mangled and Haemorrhage through Sloppy Butcher: Mangled slows their healing, Haemorrhage drains partial healing progress once they stop, and Sloppy Butcher makes that loss faster. A Nurse's Calling shows the auras of survivors healing or being healed within {{A Nurse's Calling|aurarevealdistance}} m, and inside your terror radius Coulrophobia makes them heal {{Coulrophobia|healpenalty%}}% slower with faster skill checks. While survivors stay injured, Thanatophobia slows everyone's repairs, cleansing and hook sabotage by {{Thanatophobia|actionspeedpenaltypersurvivor%}}% for each injured, downed or hooked survivor.
tips: Small no-commentary channel; the description lists all four perks and the add-ons ("Swift Hunt" - Blood and "Windstorm" - Blood).
Sloppy Butcher only applies on basic-attack hits.

builds.title: Unhookable (No Mither + Conviction)
builds.summary: Recover on the ground, turn that recovery into wiggle progress on pick-up, and fight to get free before you reach a hook.
builds.details: No Mither leaves you injured and Broken from the start of the trial; it also makes you recover {{No Mither|extrarecover%}}% faster and lets you fully recover on your own. Once you have finished healing another survivor, Conviction lets you press the Active Ability button while downed with at least {{Conviction|recoverprogressneeded%}}% recovery to get up instantly, but you are downed again {{Conviction|effectduration}} s later. If the killer picks you up, Flip-Flop adds {{Flip-Flop|recoveryratio%}}% of your recovery to your wiggle (up to {{Flip-Flop|maxwiggle%}}%), and Boil Over makes your wiggle {{Boil Over|wiggleintensity%}}% stronger, stops the killer seeing hook auras within {{Boil Over|hookaurablockrange}} m and adds {{Boil Over|fallextrawiggle%}}% of your current wiggle whenever they fall from a height.
tips: Conviction needs you to have finished healing another survivor first, so heal a teammate early.
Going down far from hooks gives you more time to wiggle, and drops from a height add Boil Over progress.
Played as a duo in the video.

builds.title: Power Struggle Classic
builds.summary: Down yourself silently next to a pallet, bank recovery, then stun the killer with that pallet after the pick-up.
builds.details: While injured, crouched and idle, Plot Twist lets you press the Secondary Ability button to be downed silently; once per trial, while downed that way, you leave no blood or grunts and recover {{Plot Twist|recoveryspeedincrease%}}% faster, and Unbreakable adds {{Unbreakable|recoverextraspeed%}}% faster recovery whenever you are downed. When the killer picks you up, Flip-Flop adds {{Flip-Flop|recoveryratio%}}% of your recovery to your wiggle (up to {{Flip-Flop|maxwiggle%}}%), and with at least {{Power Struggle|wigglerequired%}}% wiggle next to an upright pallet, Power Struggle lets you drop it to stun the killer. Power Struggle also shows you upright pallet auras while you are downed, so you can pick your spot.
tips: Recover as far as possible before the killer arrives.
Power Struggle only works next to an upright pallet, so plan where you go down.
If you fully recover from a Plot Twist down instead, you are healed instantly and gain {{Plot Twist|haste%}}% Haste for {{Plot Twist|hasteduration}} s.
Unbreakable's once-per-trial full recovery only applies when the killer downs you; Plot Twist has its own.

builds.title: Power Struggle + Lend a Hand
builds.summary: A team version of the pallet-stun escape: Lend a Hand's healing charges, Flip-Flop's wiggle head start and Power Struggle's pallet stun.
builds.details: After you bless or cleanse a totem, Lend a Hand lets you press the Secondary Ability button while healing a teammate to give them {{Lend a Hand|permanenthealingvalue}} permanent healing charges, once per survivor; the creators build the strategy around those charges. When the killer picks you up, Flip-Flop adds {{Flip-Flop|recoveryratio%}}% of your recovery progress to your wiggle (up to {{Flip-Flop|maxwiggle%}}%), and once you have at least {{Power Struggle|wigglerequired%}}% wiggle next to an upright pallet, Power Struggle lets you drop it to stun the killer. Unbreakable makes you recover {{Unbreakable|recoverextraspeed%}}% faster while downed and lets you fully recover once per trial; the source video argues this combination made Power Struggle meta in July 2026.
tips: Lend a Hand only works while you heal another survivor, once per survivor, so the team has to heal each other.
The creator suggests a med-kit for picking a teammate up from the ground.
Unbreakable's full recovery only applies when the killer downs you.

builds.title: Blind-and-Run Flashlight Bully
builds.summary: Residual Manifest turns each blind into Blindness, Champion of Light adds Hindered when off cooldown, and any stun hides your trail.
builds.details: While you are using a flashlight, Champion of Light gives you {{Champion of Light|haste%}}% Haste, and when you blind the killer they get {{Champion of Light|hindered%}}% Hindered for {{Champion of Light|hinderedduration}} s ({{Champion of Light|cooldown}} s cooldown) plus Blindness for {{Residual Manifest|blindnessduration}} s from Residual Manifest, which stops their aura reading. Pallet-stunning the killer gives you {{Smash Hit|haste%}}% Haste for {{Smash Hit|hasteduration}} s and Exhausted through Smash Hit, and any stun makes Parental Guidance hide your scratch marks, blood pools and grunts of pain for {{Parental Guidance|stealthduration}} s. Seine presents it as the most annoying survivor build he could make.
tips: Bring the strongest flashlight you own.
Residual Manifest lets you rummage a chest once, and that first rummage gives an uncommon flashlight.
Champion of Light's Hindered has a cooldown; Residual Manifest's Blindness does not.

builds.title: Flashlight Save Build
builds.summary: Get to pick-ups fast with Background Player, then make each blind cost the killer Blindness and, off cooldown, Hindered.
builds.details: Whenever the killer picks up another survivor, Background Player gives you {{Background Player|haste%}}% Haste for {{Background Player|hasteduration}} s if you start running within {{Background Player|effectduration}} s, then leaves you Exhausted. When you blind the killer, Champion of Light gives them {{Champion of Light|hindered%}}% Hindered for {{Champion of Light|hinderedduration}} s and Residual Manifest gives them Blindness for {{Residual Manifest|blindnessduration}} s, and Champion of Light also gives you {{Champion of Light|haste%}}% Haste while you use the flashlight. Empathy shows injured survivors within {{Empathy|aurarevealdistance}} m, which tells you where chases are likely happening. This is the guide's solo-queue variant; with a coordinated team, swap Empathy for Bond as its main build does.
tips: Guide recommends a high-rarity flashlight with battery and lens add-ons.
Background Player cannot trigger while you are Exhausted, so any Exhausted you pick up beforehand costs you the sprint to the pick-up.

builds.title: Sabo Squad
builds.summary: Find and sabotage the hook the killer is heading for while Breakout speeds up the carried survivor's wiggle.
builds.details: Within {{Saboteur|revealhookdistance}} m of where a teammate was picked up and is being carried, Saboteur shows you the auras of hooks and Scourge Hooks, and it lets you sabotage hooks ({{Saboteur|cooldown}} s cooldown), and Background Player gives {{Background Player|haste%}}% Haste for {{Background Player|hasteduration}} s if you start running within {{Background Player|effectduration}} s of the pick-up. Within {{Breakout|requireddistance}} m of the carried survivor, Breakout gives you {{Breakout|haste%}}% Haste and makes them wiggle {{Breakout|extrawiggle%}}% faster. Flashbang, crafted in a locker once {{Flashbang|requiredprogresstocraft%}}% of generators are repaired, blinds anyone nearby who is looking at the detonation and alerts the killer.
tips: The guide pairs it with a sabotage toolbox.
The guide names Midwich Elementary School and the Raccoon City police station among the maps where it works best.

builds.title: Locker Jukes and Head On Stuns
builds.summary: The classic locker build: fake the entry, hide for real without a sound, then burst out for a stun.
builds.details: Deception turns a fast-enter into a fake: you stay outside the locker, the killer is alerted, and you leave no scratch marks or blood for {{Deception|noscratchmarksduration}} s ({{Deception|cooldown}} s cooldown). Quick & Quiet makes real locker entries and vaults silent so the killer is not alerted ({{Quick & Quiet|cooldown}} s cooldown), which leaves them guessing which locker you used. After {{Head On|hiderequiredduration}} s inside, Head On lets you fast-exit to stun a killer within {{Head On|lockerstunrange}} m for {{Head On|lockerstunduration}} s, and Flashbang, crafted in a locker once {{Flashbang|requiredprogresstocraft%}}% of generators are repaired, blinds anyone nearby who is looking at the detonation. It is tagged meta because it is among the most-recorded survivor loadouts on NightLight (see evidence).
tips: Head On needs {{Head On|hiderequiredduration}} s in the locker first and leaves you Exhausted for {{Head On|exhaustedduration}} s.
Deception alerts the killer on purpose; Quick & Quiet hides the real entry.
builds.evidence: NightLight.gg community stats (patch window 10.1.0 onward, 2026-08-25 to 2026-11-16): #12 most-used survivor build, 285 recorded loadouts (0.17% of all survivor loadouts); 84 escapes (29.5% escape rate).

builds.title: Quad-Stun Menace
builds.summary: Locker stun, vault stun, generator stun and a blind, all in one build.
builds.details: Head On stuns the killer for {{Head On|lockerstunduration}} s if they are within {{Head On|lockerstunrange}} m when you fast-exit a locker after hiding {{Head On|hiderequiredduration}} s, then leaves you Exhausted. Last Stand gives one fast-vault stun per trial, but only after you have spent {{Last Stand|activationtime}} s hiding inside the killer's terror radius, and only if they are within {{Last Stand|stunrange}} m. Once {{Blast Mine|requiredprogress%}}% of generators are repaired, Blast Mine can trap a generator for {{Blast Mine|trapduration}} s so the killer is stunned for {{Blast Mine|stunblindduration}} s when they damage it, and Flashbang can be crafted in a locker to blind anyone nearby who is looking at the detonation. The build gives up objective help to interrupt the killer as often as possible, and the creator titles it the most toxic survivor build.
tips: Blast Mine ({{Blast Mine|requiredprogress%}}%) and Flashbang ({{Flashbang|requiredprogresstocraft%}}%) both need that share of generators repaired first, so repair early.
Last Stand works only once per trial and only after {{Last Stand|activationtime}} s of hiding in the terror radius.
Every survivor sees a trapped generator's aura while Blast Mine is armed.

builds.title: Gen-Kick Punisher
builds.summary: Trap a generator, leave a Mirrored Illusion beside it as bait, and punish each blind with Blindness and, off cooldown, Hindered.
builds.details: Once {{Blast Mine|requiredprogress%}}% of generators are repaired, Blast Mine traps a generator for {{Blast Mine|trapduration}} s: when the killer damages it they are stunned for {{Blast Mine|stunblindduration}} s, and anyone nearby looking at the detonation is blinded. Mirrored Illusion, available after {{Mirrored Illusion|requiredprogress%}}% of generators are repaired, places a static illusion next to a generator (or a chest, gate switch or totem) for {{Mirrored Illusion|huskduration}} s to draw the killer in. Whenever you blind the killer, Residual Manifest gives them Blindness for {{Residual Manifest|blindnessduration}} s and Champion of Light gives them {{Champion of Light|hindered%}}% Hindered for {{Champion of Light|hinderedduration}} s; the video counts on the mine's blind for this, and a flashlight is the sure way to trigger them.
tips: Residual Manifest lets you rummage one chest for an uncommon flashlight, which also gives you Champion of Light's Haste while you use it.
Every survivor sees the trapped generator's aura while Blast Mine is armed.

builds.title: Blind Everything
builds.summary: Whenever you blind the killer, Residual Manifest adds {{Residual Manifest|blindnessduration}} s of Blindness and Champion of Light adds Hindered on a cooldown; Blast Mine and Flashbang add more ways to blind them.
builds.details: Residual Manifest gives the killer Blindness for {{Residual Manifest|blindnessduration}} s whenever you blind them, which stops them reading Auras, and the first Chest you rummage holds an uncommon Flashlight. Champion of Light gives you {{Champion of Light|haste%}}% Haste while you are using a Flashlight, and blinding the killer gives them {{Champion of Light|hindered%}}% Hindered for {{Champion of Light|hinderedduration}} s (cooldown {{Champion of Light|cooldown}} s). After repairing {{Blast Mine|requiredprogress%}}% of Generators, Blast Mine lets you trap a generator with the Secondary Ability button so the killer is stunned for {{Blast Mine|stunblindduration}} s when they damage it, and after repairing {{Flashbang|requiredprogresstocraft%}}% of Generators, Flashbang lets you craft a Flashbang in a Locker with the Active Ability button. Both detonations blind everyone nearby who is looking at them (the Flashbang also alerts the killer); Seine calls Residual Manifest the strongest survivor perk nobody uses.
tips: Blast Mine and Flashbang only blind a killer who is looking at the detonation; the Blast Mine stun happens either way.
Champion of Light's Hindered has a {{Champion of Light|cooldown}} s cooldown, while Residual Manifest adds Blindness on each blind you land.
Find a Chest early: the first one you rummage gives you the Flashlight that Residual Manifest promises.
Video loadout: purple flashlight with Long Life Battery and Low Amp Filament.

builds.title: Boon Gen Rush
builds.summary: Bless a totem so generators in its range repair faster and regress more slowly; Overzealous adds a repair bonus after each bless or cleanse; Fast Track turns unhooks into bonus generator progress.
builds.details: Boon: Steadfast makes generators within the Boon's range regress {{Boon: Steadfast|regressionmodifier}}% slower and lets Survivors repair them {{Boon: Steadfast|repairspeedmodifier}}% faster, and Survivors in range see those generators' Auras. Overzealous makes you repair {{Overzealous|actionspeedbonus%}}% faster after you bless or cleanse a Totem ({{Overzealous|doubledactionspeedbonus%}}% if it was a Hex Totem) until you take damage, and Flow State earns a Token each time a Generator is completed (up to {{Flow State|maxtokens}}), each one making you bless, cleanse, heal and unhook {{Flow State|actionspeedbuff%}}% faster. Fast Track earns a Token whenever you unhook another Survivor (up to {{Fast Track|maxtokens}}) and spends all of them when you hit a great basic Skill Check while repairing, adding {{Fast Track|bonuspertoken%}}% permanent progress per Token. Seine presents it as the October 2026 gen-rush meta and argues it is very hard to beat when a whole team commits to it.
tips: Overzealous ends when you take damage; bless or cleanse another Totem to turn it back on.
Steadfast, Overzealous and a toolbox are all repair-speed bonuses, so under diminishing returns the largest counts in full, the second at half and the third at a quarter.
Fast Track spends its Tokens automatically on your next great basic Skill Check while repairing, so the bonus lands on whatever generator you are working on.
Video loadout: Commodious Toolbox with Brand New Part.

builds.title: Skill-Check Gen Rush
builds.summary: Four different repair boosts: Deja Vu on a cluster of generators, bonus Skill Check progress from Stake Out and Hyperfocus, and Built to Last refilling a depleted item such as a toolbox in a Locker.
builds.details: Deja Vu shows the Auras of the {{Deja Vu|generatorsshown}} Generators closest to each other and makes you repair them {{Deja Vu|repairspeed%}}% faster. Stake Out earns a Token (up to {{Stake Out|maxtokens}}) after you hide for {{Stake Out|tokenchargetime}} s within {{Stake Out|tokenchargerange}} m of the killer while in their Terror Radius; while you hold one, basic Skill Checks are replaced by special Skill Checks worth {{Stake Out|additionalprogressgained}}% more progress, and each special Skill Check you hit or miss spends a Token. Hyperfocus earns a Token for each great basic Skill Check (up to {{Hyperfocus|maxtokens}}); per Token, basic Skill Checks appear {{Hyperfocus|skillcheckbonuschance%}}% more often, spin {{Hyperfocus|skillcheckspeedincrease%}}% faster and give {{Hyperfocus|skillcheckbonuspertoken%}}% more progress on a great, and all Tokens are lost on a missed basic Skill Check, a good Skill Check or when you stop repairing or healing. Built to Last recharges a depleted item to {{Built to Last|initialrefill%}}% after {{Built to Last|requiredduration}} s in a Locker, {{Built to Last|refilldiminishing%}}% fewer Charges each time, and PlayHub recommends the same four perks as its generator build.
tips: By their wording, Stake Out and Hyperfocus take turns: as long as you have a Stake Out Token your basic Skill Checks are replaced by special ones, and Hyperfocus only counts and boosts basic Skill Checks, though hitting a good special Skill Check still makes you lose all Hyperfocus Tokens.
Hyperfocus resets on a good Skill Check, so it only pays off while you keep hitting greats.
Built to Last refills {{Built to Last|refilldiminishing%}}% fewer Charges with each use, so the first refill is the biggest.
Also listed as the Generator Build in PlayHub's 2026 survivor guide (https://playhub.com/blog/dead-by-daylight/best-survivor-builds-602668).
builds.evidence: NightLight.gg community stats (patch window 10.1.0 onward, 2026-08-25 to 2026-11-16): #13 most-used survivor build, 269 recorded loadouts (0.16% of all survivor loadouts); 82 escapes (30.5% escape rate).

builds.title: Wiggle Build
builds.summary: A wiggle loadout for both sides of a carry: Boil Over and Flip-Flop help you wiggle free, while Background Player and Breakout get you to a carried teammate fast and speed up their wiggle.
builds.details: While you are carried, Boil Over makes your wiggle {{Boil Over|wiggleintensity%}}% stronger, stops the killer seeing Hook Auras within {{Boil Over|hookaurablockrange}} m and adds {{Boil Over|fallextrawiggle%}}% of your current wiggle progress whenever the killer falls from a height. Flip-Flop adds {{Flip-Flop|recoveryratio%}}% of your recovery progress to your wiggle progress when the killer picks you up, up to {{Flip-Flop|maxwiggle%}}%. When the killer picks up a teammate, Background Player gives you {{Background Player|haste%}}% Haste for {{Background Player|hasteduration}} s if you start running within {{Background Player|effectduration}} s (then Exhausted for {{Background Player|exhaustedduration}} s), and within {{Breakout|requireddistance}} m of the carried Survivor, Breakout gives you {{Breakout|haste%}}% Haste and makes them wiggle {{Breakout|extrawiggle%}}% faster. The aim is to turn carries into wiggle escapes instead of hooks.
tips: Recover while you are slugged: Flip-Flop turns that recovery progress into wiggle progress when you are picked up.
Breakout only works within {{Breakout|requireddistance}} m of the carried Survivor, so stay close behind the killer.
Background Player's sprint starts when you start running in the {{Background Player|effectduration}} s after a pick-up, so you can choose the moment to go.
The creator (a small channel that lists the perks in the video description) runs it with a sabotage toolbox.

builds.title: Unpunishable Bodyblocker
builds.summary: Take protection hits on purpose: Duty of Care hastes nearby teammates, Overcome helps you get away, and {{Mettle of Man|tokensneeded}} protection hits arm Mettle of Man to shrug off a down.
builds.details: Whenever you take a protection hit while healthy, Duty of Care gives other Survivors within {{Duty of Care|maxdistance}} m {{Duty of Care|haste%}}% Haste for {{Duty of Care|hasteduration}} s, and when you take damage, Overcome makes you keep the speed boost {{Overcome|extraboosttime}} s longer (then Exhausted for {{Overcome|exhaustionduration}} s). After {{Mettle of Man|tokensneeded}} protection hits, Mettle of Man makes the next down the killer would give you while injured deal no damage; it also makes you more likely to be the Obsession, and when you become healthy the killer sees your Aura while you are at least {{Mettle of Man|aurarevealdistance}} m away.
