We're Gonna Live Forever heals downed Survivors {{We're Gonna Live Forever|healspeedincrease%}}% faster and gives them Endurance for {{We're Gonna Live Forever|enduranceduration}} s when you finish (cooldown {{We're Gonna Live Forever|endurancecooldownduration}} s), so you can pick up whoever the killer leaves on the ground. The killer keeps hitting the Survivor they did not want to hit, which is what makes it toxic.
tips: Duty of Care only triggers on protection hits you take while healthy.
Mettle of Man only saves you while you are injured; once you are healthy again, the killer sees your Aura while you are at least {{Mettle of Man|aurarevealdistance}} m away.
Overcome makes you Exhausted for {{Overcome|exhaustionduration}} s, and Exhaustion perks cannot trigger while you are Exhausted, so it will not help on a second hit inside that time.
We're Gonna Live Forever's Endurance has a {{We're Gonna Live Forever|endurancecooldownduration}} s cooldown, so plan who you pick up first.

builds.title: Stun Build (Payback)
builds.summary: Stun the killer from a Locker with Head On, at a trapped generator with Blast Mine and with Pallets you reset using Any Means Necessary, while Exultation upgrades your item on Pallet stuns.
builds.details: Head On stuns the killer for {{Head On|lockerstunduration}} s if they are within {{Head On|lockerstunrange}} m when you fast-exit a Locker after hiding for {{Head On|hiderequiredduration}} s (then Exhausted for {{Head On|exhaustedduration}} s), and after you have repaired {{Blast Mine|requiredprogress%}}% of Generators, Blast Mine traps a generator with the Secondary Ability button so the killer is stunned for {{Blast Mine|stunblindduration}} s when they damage it. Any Means Necessary shows the Auras of dropped Pallets; next to one, using the Active Ability button for {{Any Means Necessary|actiontimerequired}} s resets it so you can stun the killer with it again. Whenever you Pallet-stun the killer, Exultation upgrades your item to the next rarity if possible and, if it was upgraded, recharges {{Exultation|itemrecharge%}}% of its Charges (cooldown {{Exultation|cooldown}} s). Game Rant files it under getting payback on the killer.
tips: Exultation cannot upgrade an item that is already at the top rarity, and without an upgrade it does not recharge it.
Head On only works after {{Head On|hiderequiredduration}} s in the Locker and only if the killer is within {{Head On|lockerstunrange}} m as you fast-exit.
Blast Mine stuns the killer whether or not they look at it; only its blind needs them to be looking at the detonation.
Reset Pallets at loops you plan to run again; Any Means Necessary shows you the Auras of dropped Pallets.

builds.title: Trap-Everything Decoy Build
builds.summary: Trap Pallets with Chemical Trap, Windows with Bada Bada Boom and generators with Blast Mine, then place Mirrored Illusion's static decoys to try to lure the killer toward them.
builds.details: After you have repaired {{Chemical Trap|requiredprogress%}}% of Generators, Chemical Trap traps a dropped Pallet for {{Chemical Trap|trapduration}} s and breaking it gives the killer {{Chemical Trap|hinder%}}% Hindered for {{Chemical Trap|hinderduration}} s; Bada Bada Boom does the same to a Window the killer vaults ({{Bada Bada Boom|traphinder%}}% Hindered for {{Bada Bada Boom|hinderduration}} s, trap lasting {{Bada Bada Boom|trapduration}} s, unlocked after {{Bada Bada Boom|requiredgeneratorprogress%}}% of Generators). Blast Mine unlocks after {{Blast Mine|requiredprogress%}}% of Generators and traps a generator for {{Blast Mine|trapduration}} s: when the killer damages it, they are stunned for {{Blast Mine|stunblindduration}} s and everyone nearby looking at the detonation is blinded. Mirrored Illusion (after {{Mirrored Illusion|requiredprogress%}}% of Generators) creates a static illusion for {{Mirrored Illusion|huskduration}} s next to a Chest, Exit Gate Switch, Generator or Totem; all four perks use the Secondary Ability button, and all Survivors see the Aura of each trapped Pallet, Window or Generator while the trap lasts. Seine describes it as the most annoying survivor strategy.
tips: Swap Bada Bada Boom for Last Stand if you prefer; it is the video's listed alternative.
Mirrored Illusion can be placed next to a generator, so a Blast-Mined generator is the most direct place to try to bait the killer with one.
Teammates see your trapped Pallets, Windows and Generators, so they can lead chases through them too.
Blast Mine's stun works even if the killer is not looking; only its blind needs them to look at the detonation.

builds.title: Most-Used Killer Build: Kick-and-Hook Regression
builds.summary: Corrupt Intervention stalls the start; then Pop Goes the Weasel boosts kicks after hooks, Eruption explodes kicked generators on downs and Pain Resonance hits the leading generator on each Survivor's first Scourge Hook.
builds.details: Corrupt Intervention blocks the {{Corrupt Intervention|generatorsblocked}} Generators farthest from you for {{Corrupt Intervention|generatorblockduration}} s at the start of the trial, or until you down a Survivor. Pop Goes the Weasel: for {{Pop Goes the Weasel|activeduration}} s after you hook a Survivor, kicking a generator makes it explode and lose {{Pop Goes the Weasel|extrageneratordamage%}}% more progress; Eruption: once you have damaged generators, downing a Survivor makes all generators damaged this way explode, lose {{Eruption|generatorregress%}}% progress and start regressing, while Survivors repairing them scream and show their Auras for {{Eruption|aurarevealduration}} s (cooldown {{Eruption|cooldown}} s). Scourge Hook: Pain Resonance turns random hooks into Scourge Hooks at the start and gives you {{Scourge Hook: Pain Resonance|startingtokens}} Tokens; the first time each Survivor is hooked on one, a Token is spent and the generator with the most progress explodes, loses {{Scourge Hook: Pain Resonance|generatorregression%}}% progress and starts regressing. None of the four depend on a killer power, so the loadout fits any killer.
tips: Pop only works in the {{Pop Goes the Weasel|activeduration}} s after a hook, so head to a generator right after hooking and kick it.
Eruption only affects generators you have already damaged, so kick generators before you commit to a chase.
Pain Resonance only fires the first time each Survivor is hooked on a Scourge Hook, and it has {{Scourge Hook: Pain Resonance|startingtokens}} Tokens in total.
A generator can take at most 8 regression events per trial (a kick with Pop counts as one), so spread your kicks across generators.
builds.evidence: NightLight.gg community stats (patch window 10.1.0 onward, 2026-08-25 to 2026-11-16): #1 most-used killer build, 357 recorded loadouts (1.2% of all killer loadouts); 522 of 779 tracked survivors killed (67.0% kill rate). In the same window, Scourge Hook: Pain Resonance alone appears in 31.08% of recorded killer loadouts, and this build is used almost three times as often as the next tracked build.

builds.title: Aura Hunter (Celestial Witness + Lethal Pursuer)
builds.summary: Second most-used tracked killer build: four aura perks, with Celestial Witness and Nemesis feeding each other through the Obsession, and no generator slowdown.
builds.details: Lethal Pursuer shows every Survivor's Aura for {{Lethal Pursuer|aurarevealduration}} s at the start and makes each timed Aura reveal {{Lethal Pursuer|bonusaurarevealduration}} s longer, and A Nurse's Calling shows you Survivors within {{A Nurse's Calling|aurarevealdistance}} m who are healing or being healed. Every {{Celestial Witness|timer}} s, Celestial Witness shows the Obsession's Aura for {{Celestial Witness|auraduration}} s if they are at least {{Celestial Witness|distance}} m away; otherwise the farthest Survivor becomes the Obsession. Nemesis makes any Survivor who blinds you or stuns you with a Locker or Pallet the Obsession. Whenever a Survivor becomes the Obsession, including through Celestial Witness, Nemesis gives them Oblivious for {{Nemesis|obliviousduration}} s and shows you their Aura for {{Nemesis|aurarevealduration}} s.
tips: Chasing the Obsession up close is not wasted: if they are within {{Celestial Witness|distance}} m when Celestial Witness checks every {{Celestial Witness|timer}} s, the Obsession passes to the farthest Survivor, and Nemesis then reveals that Survivor and makes them Oblivious.
Lethal Pursuer adds {{Lethal Pursuer|bonusaurarevealduration}} s to the Celestial Witness and Nemesis reveals as well as to its own opening reveal.
A Nurse's Calling only shows Survivors while they heal or are being healed within {{A Nurse's Calling|aurarevealdistance}} m.
builds.evidence: NightLight.gg community stats (patch window 10.1.0 onward, 2026-08-25 to 2026-11-16): #2 most-used killer build, 132 recorded loadouts (0.45% of all killer loadouts); 193 of 282 tracked survivors killed (68.4% kill rate). Overall killer kill rate in the same data: about 48%. Celestial Witness pick rate: 5.92%.

builds.title: Wallhack Stack (Deerstalker + Gearhead)
builds.summary: Third most-used tracked killer build: four aura perks, including Deerstalker's two-way Aura swap and Gearhead's reveals on good Skill Checks after a hit.
builds.details: Lethal Pursuer shows all Survivors for {{Lethal Pursuer|aurarevealduration}} s at the start and adds {{Lethal Pursuer|bonusaurarevealduration}} s to each timed Aura reveal, and A Nurse's Calling shows you Survivors within {{A Nurse's Calling|aurarevealdistance}} m who are healing or being healed. Every {{Deerstalker|revealtimeintervals}} s, Deerstalker shows your Aura for {{Deerstalker|revealduration}} s to the Survivor with the least time in chase, and you see their Aura for as long as they see yours. For {{Gearhead|effectduration}} s after any Survivor takes damage, Gearhead shows you, for {{Gearhead|aurarevealduration}} s, any Survivor repairing a generator who hits a good basic Skill Check. With no slowdown at all, it suits killers who can quickly reach what they see.
tips: Deerstalker also shows that Survivor where you are, so they get a warning too.
Gearhead only counts good basic Skill Checks on generators, and only in the {{Gearhead|effectduration}} s after a Survivor takes damage.
Lethal Pursuer makes each Gearhead reveal {{Lethal Pursuer|bonusaurarevealduration}} s longer.
builds.evidence: NightLight.gg community stats (patch window 10.1.0 onward, 2026-08-25 to 2026-11-16): #3 most-used killer build, 108 recorded loadouts (0.36% of all killer loadouts); 156 of 249 tracked survivors killed (62.7% kill rate).

builds.title: Barbecue and Dead Man's Switch
builds.summary: On hooks, Barbecue & Chili shows far-away Survivors and Dead Man's Switch blocks the next generator someone leaves; each Survivor's first Scourge Hook also makes Pain Resonance explode the leading generator.
builds.details: Whenever you hook a Survivor, Barbecue & Chili shows you for {{Barbecue & Chili|aurarevealduration}} s the Auras of all Survivors at least {{Barbecue & Chili|mindistancefromhook}} m from the hooked one, and Lethal Pursuer makes that reveal {{Lethal Pursuer|bonusaurarevealduration}} s longer on top of showing everyone for {{Lethal Pursuer|aurarevealduration}} s at the start. After a hook, Dead Man's Switch blocks the next generator that any Survivor stops repairing for more than {{Dead Man’s Switch|generatorreleaseduration}} s, for {{Dead Man’s Switch|generatorblockduration}} s (cooldown {{Dead Man’s Switch|cooldown}} s). The first time each Survivor is hooked on a Scourge Hook, Pain Resonance spends one of its {{Scourge Hook: Pain Resonance|startingtokens}} Tokens and makes the generator with the most progress explode, lose {{Scourge Hook: Pain Resonance|generatorregression%}}% progress and start regressing, and Survivors repairing it scream.
tips: Use Scourge Hooks when you can: Pain Resonance only triggers on each Survivor's first Scourge Hook.
After a hook, use the Barbecue & Chili read to choose your next target while Dead Man's Switch waits for the next Survivor to leave a generator.
builds.evidence: NightLight.gg community stats (patch window 10.1.0 onward, 2026-08-25 to 2026-11-16): #6 most-used killer build, 67 recorded loadouts (0.23% of all killer loadouts); 80 of 163 tracked survivors killed (49.1% kill rate). Its tracked kill rate sits close to the overall killer average in the same data.

builds.title: Tracked Hex Stack (Ruin, Undying, Thrill, Pentimento)
builds.summary: The most-used all-Hex loadout in tracked matches: Ruin makes unattended generators regress, Undying and Thrill of the Hunt protect the Hexes, and Pentimento punishes cleansing.
builds.details: Hex: Ruin and Hex: Undying each light a Dull Totem when the trial starts; Ruin makes any generator that is not being repaired regress at {{Hex: Ruin|regressionspeed%}}% speed, and when another Hex Totem is blessed or cleansed, that Hex moves onto Undying's Totem and keeps its Tokens. Hex: Thrill of the Hunt lights a Dull Totem the first time you hook a Survivor, and each hook blocks all Hex Totems for {{Hex: Thrill of the Hunt|blockdurationpertoken}} s per lit Hex Totem, while Undying also shows you Survivors within {{Hex: Undying|aurarevealdistance}} m of Dull Totems. Hex: Pentimento shows you cleansed Totems and lets you rekindle each once: while a Totem is rekindled, Survivors heal and repair {{Hex: Pentimento|baseactionspeedpenalty%}}% slower, plus {{Hex: Pentimento|actionspeedpenaltypertotem%}}% for each additional rekindled Totem, and Survivors within {{Hex: Pentimento|totemaurareveadistance}} m see rekindled Totems. Survivors have to choose between spending time on totems and playing against Ruin's regression.
tips: Thrill of the Hunt only lights on your first hook if a Dull Totem is still left at that moment.
Thrill's hook block grows with each lit Hex Totem, so it is strongest while Ruin and Undying are both up.
If all {{Hex: Pentimento|maxtokens}} Totems are rekindled at the same time, they become blocked.
Undying's reveal within {{Hex: Undying|aurarevealdistance}} m of Dull Totems points you to Survivors near Dull Totems, for example ones about to cleanse them.
builds.evidence: NightLight.gg community stats (patch window 10.1.0 onward, 2026-08-25 to 2026-11-16): #8 most-used killer build, 57 recorded loadouts (0.19% of all killer loadouts); 82 of 131 tracked survivors killed (62.6% kill rate).

builds.title: Lay Waste Regression
builds.summary: The standard regression core of Corrupt Intervention, Eruption and Pain Resonance, plus Lay Waste, which makes a generator you kick regress faster the more Charges it has.
builds.details: Whenever you damage a generator, Lay Waste makes it regress {{Lay Waste|fasterregression}}% faster for each Charge it has (cooldown {{Lay Waste|cooldown}} s), and the same kick marks it for Eruption, which makes it explode, lose {{Eruption|generatorregress%}}% progress and start regressing when you down a Survivor (cooldown {{Eruption|cooldown}} s). The first time each Survivor is hooked on a Scourge Hook, Pain Resonance makes the generator with the most progress explode and lose {{Scourge Hook: Pain Resonance|generatorregression%}}% progress, and Corrupt Intervention blocks the {{Corrupt Intervention|generatorsblocked}} farthest generators for {{Corrupt Intervention|generatorblockduration}} s at the start or until you down a Survivor. Lay Waste only changes how fast a kicked generator regresses, so it pays off most on generators that already have a lot of progress.
tips: Eruption's down also makes Survivors on those generators scream and shows their Auras for {{Eruption|aurarevealduration}} s.
Lay Waste and Eruption both work from the kick, but Lay Waste has its own {{Lay Waste|cooldown}} s cooldown.
Corrupt Intervention ends early at your first down, which is also your first chance to trigger Eruption.
builds.evidence: NightLight.gg community stats (patch window 10.1.0 onward, 2026-08-25 to 2026-11-16): #9 most-used killer build, 56 recorded loadouts (0.19% of all killer loadouts); 78 of 124 tracked survivors killed (62.9% kill rate). It is the most-used full four-perk build containing Lay Waste, which has a 4.04% pick rate in the same window.

builds.title: Most-Used Survivor Build: Second-Chance Looper
builds.summary: The most common tracked survivor loadout: Five Moves Ahead and Resilience for chases, with Decisive Strike and Dead Hard as protection after being unhooked.
builds.details: While you are in the killer's Terror Radius or in chase, Five Moves Ahead shows the Auras of the {{Five Moves Ahead|palletwindowauracount}} closest Pallets and lets you start moving {{Five Moves Ahead|actionspeedbuff%}}% earlier after dropping a Pallet, with a {{Five Moves Ahead|cooldown}} s cooldown after each drop. Resilience makes you {{Resilience|actionspeed%}}% faster at vaulting, repairing, healing, unhooking and several other actions while injured. For {{Decisive Strike|effectduration}} s after you are unhooked, until all Generators are completed, Decisive Strike gives you a special Skill Check when the killer picks you up, and hitting it stuns them for {{Decisive Strike|stunduration}} s (once per trial, disabled by conspicuous actions). After an unhook, Dead Hard lets you press the Active Ability button when injured and running to gain Endurance for {{Dead Hard|enduranceduration}} s, and you become Exhausted for {{Dead Hard|exhaustedduration}} s.
tips: Decisive Strike works once per trial and only until all Generators are completed.
Dead Hard's Endurance lasts only {{Dead Hard|enduranceduration}} s, so press the button just before the hit lands.
Dead Hard, like Resilience, only works while you are injured.
builds.evidence: NightLight.gg community stats (patch window 10.1.0 onward, 2026-08-25 to 2026-11-16): #1 most-used survivor build, 750 recorded loadouts (0.45% of all survivor loadouts); 295 escapes (39.3% escape rate). Decisive Strike appears in 16.27% and Dead Hard in 18.04% of recorded survivor loadouts.

builds.title: Vault Meta (Lithe, Windows, Finesse)
builds.summary: Second most-used tracked survivor build, built around windows: Windows of Opportunity finds them, Finesse and Resilience speed up vaults, and Lithe turns medium and fast vaults into a sprint.
builds.details: Windows of Opportunity shows the Auras of Windows within {{Windows of Opportunity|vaultablesrevealdistance}} m; it also makes you vault Windows faster and goes on a {{Windows of Opportunity|cooldown}} s cooldown after each Window vault. Finesse makes you fast-vault {{Finesse|vaultspeedincrease%}}% faster while healthy (cooldown {{Finesse|cooldown}} s after each fast vault), and Resilience makes you vault, repair, heal and do several other actions {{Resilience|actionspeed%}}% faster while injured. Lithe gives you {{Lithe|haste%}}% Haste for {{Lithe|hasteduration}} s whenever you medium or fast-vault, then Exhausted for {{Lithe|exhaustionduration}} s.
tips: Finesse works only while healthy and Resilience only while injured, so the two never apply together.
Vault-speed bonuses fall under diminishing returns: when Windows of Opportunity applies together with Finesse or Resilience, the smaller bonus counts at half.
Lithe makes you Exhausted for {{Lithe|exhaustionduration}} s, and Exhaustion perks cannot trigger while you are Exhausted.
builds.evidence: NightLight.gg community stats (patch window 10.1.0 onward, 2026-08-25 to 2026-11-16): #2 most-used survivor build, 571 recorded loadouts (0.35% of all survivor loadouts); 169 escapes (29.6% escape rate). Lithe is the most-picked survivor perk in the data at 24.9%. This build's tracked escape rate is lower than that of most other top builds.

builds.title: Pallet-and-Window Looper
builds.summary: Third most-used tracked survivor build: Five Moves Ahead for Pallets, Finesse and Lithe for vaults, and Resilience while injured.
builds.details: In the killer's Terror Radius or in chase, Five Moves Ahead shows the {{Five Moves Ahead|palletwindowauracount}} closest Pallets and lets you start moving {{Five Moves Ahead|actionspeedbuff%}}% earlier after dropping one (cooldown {{Five Moves Ahead|cooldown}} s). Finesse makes your fast vaults {{Finesse|vaultspeedincrease%}}% faster while healthy (cooldown {{Finesse|cooldown}} s after each fast vault), Lithe gives you {{Lithe|haste%}}% Haste for {{Lithe|hasteduration}} s after a medium or fast vault (then Exhausted for {{Lithe|exhaustionduration}} s), and Resilience makes vaulting, repairing, healing and several other actions {{Resilience|actionspeed%}}% faster while injured. It is a pure chase loadout: none of the four perks does anything when you are hooked or unhooked.
tips: Finesse and Resilience never overlap: Finesse needs you healthy, Resilience needs you injured.
Five Moves Ahead only works in the Terror Radius or in chase, and goes on cooldown after each Pallet drop.
Lithe triggers on medium vaults as well as fast ones.
builds.evidence: NightLight.gg community stats (patch window 10.1.0 onward, 2026-08-25 to 2026-11-16): #3 most-used survivor build, 518 recorded loadouts (0.31% of all survivor loadouts); 191 escapes (36.9% escape rate).

builds.title: Four-Boon Totem
builds.summary: Fourth most-used tracked survivor build: one blessed Totem carrying four Boons for healing, stealth, dying-state recovery and generator repairs.
builds.details: Each Boon you equip goes onto the one Totem you bless with the Active Ability button, so all four effects share the Boon's range and are lost together if the killer snuffs it. Inside that range, Circle of Healing makes Survivors heal others {{Boon: Circle of Healing|healingspeedbonus%}}% faster without a Med-Kit and shows injured Survivors' Auras to the others, and Shadow Step removes Scratch Marks and hides Survivors' Auras from the killer until {{Boon: Shadow Step|lingerduration}} s after they leave. Exponential lets downed Survivors in range recover {{Boon: Exponential|recoverspeedboost%}}% faster and fully recover, and Steadfast makes generators in range regress {{Boon: Steadfast|regressionmodifier}}% slower and repair {{Boon: Steadfast|repairspeedmodifier}}% faster, with their Auras shown to Survivors in range. It is a whole-team support build that makes one area of the map much stronger for survivors.
tips: Bless a Totem near generators you plan to repair so Steadfast covers them.
If the Boon is snuffed, bless a Totem again to bring all four effects back.
The same Boon effect from two Totems does not stack, so coordinate with teammates who also run Boons.
builds.evidence: NightLight.gg community stats (patch window 10.1.0 onward, 2026-08-25 to 2026-11-16): #4 most-used survivor build, 456 recorded loadouts (0.28% of all survivor loadouts); 165 escapes (36.2% escape rate).

builds.title: Endgame Escape Artist (Hope + Decisive Strike)
builds.summary: Resurgence and Decisive Strike protect you after unhooks, Five Moves Ahead helps with Pallets, and Hope adds Haste once all Generators are completed, right where Decisive Strike stops working.
builds.details: Resurgence gives you {{Resurgence|healregain%}}% healing progress whenever you are unhooked, and for {{Decisive Strike|effectduration}} s after an unhook, until all Generators are completed, Decisive Strike gives you a special Skill Check when the killer picks you up, and hitting it stuns them for {{Decisive Strike|stunduration}} s (once per trial). Hope takes over where Decisive Strike stops: when all Generators are completed, you gain {{Hope|haste%}}% Haste. Five Moves Ahead shows the {{Five Moves Ahead|palletwindowauracount}} closest Pallets in the Terror Radius or in chase and lets you start moving {{Five Moves Ahead|actionspeedbuff%}}% earlier after a Pallet drop (cooldown {{Five Moves Ahead|cooldown}} s).
tips: Decisive Strike is disabled by conspicuous actions and only works once per trial.
Hope's Haste starts only when all Generators are completed.
Resurgence triggers whenever you are unhooked, not just the first time.
builds.evidence: NightLight.gg community stats (patch window 10.1.0 onward, 2026-08-25 to 2026-11-16): #6 most-used survivor build, 379 recorded loadouts (0.23% of all survivor loadouts); 310 escapes (81.8% escape rate). This is a top-ten tracked build with by far the highest escape rate in the list, roughly double that of the other top builds, but it comes from a few hundred uploads by a self-selected player base and should not be over-read.

builds.title: Anti-Slug, Anti-Tunnel Staples
builds.summary: The second-chance package against tunnelling and slugging: Decisive Strike and Dead Hard after unhooks, Unbreakable for one full self-recovery, and Resilience while injured.
builds.details: For {{Decisive Strike|effectduration}} s after you are unhooked, until all Generators are completed, Decisive Strike gives you a special Skill Check when the killer picks you up, and hitting it stuns them for {{Decisive Strike|stunduration}} s (once per trial, disabled by conspicuous actions). After an unhook, Dead Hard lets you press the Active Ability button when injured and running to gain Endurance for {{Dead Hard|enduranceduration}} s, and you become Exhausted for {{Dead Hard|exhaustedduration}} s. Unbreakable makes you recover {{Unbreakable|recoverextraspeed%}}% faster while downed and, once per trial, lets you fully recover when the killer has downed you, and Resilience makes vaulting, repairing, healing and several other actions {{Resilience|actionspeed%}}% faster while injured. Together they answer a killer who chases the unhooked Survivor straight away or leaves people on the ground.
tips: Unbreakable's full recovery works only once per trial, and only when the killer is the one who downed you.
Decisive Strike stops working once all Generators are completed.
Dead Hard's Endurance lasts only {{Dead Hard|enduranceduration}} s, so time the button press to the killer's swing.
builds.evidence: NightLight.gg community stats (patch window 10.1.0 onward, 2026-08-25 to 2026-11-16): #14 most-used survivor build, 263 recorded loadouts (0.16% of all survivor loadouts); 115 escapes (43.7% escape rate).

builds.title: Backpack Build
builds.summary: Carry a survivor around instead of hooking: Agitation and Iron Grasp keep the carry going, Starstruck makes nearby survivors Exposed and Mad Grit makes swinging while carrying cheap.
builds.details: While you carry a Survivor, Agitation gives you {{Agitation|haste%}}% Haste and a Terror Radius {{Agitation|terrorradiusincreasesize}} m larger, and Iron Grasp makes the carried Survivor wiggle {{Iron Grasp|wiggletimeincrease%}}% slower and {{Iron Grasp|wigglestrengthreduction%}}% weaker. Starstruck makes Survivors in your Terror Radius Exposed during the carry until {{Starstruck|exposedlingerduration}} s after they leave it or you drop or hook the carried Survivor (cooldown {{Starstruck|cooldown}} s), and Agitation's larger Terror Radius widens that area. While carrying, Mad Grit removes the cooldown of a missed basic attack, and each basic-attack hit on another Survivor stops the carried one gaining wiggle progress for {{Mad Grit|wigglepauseduration}} s. The joke is refusing to hook and hunting the rest of the team with a Survivor on your shoulder.
tips: Starstruck's Exposed lasts {{Starstruck|exposedlingerduration}} s after you hook, so look for another down straight after hooking.
Mad Grit only helps with basic attacks.
The video runs it on The Animatronic, but none of the four perks depend on a killer power.

builds.title: Infinite Scream Build
builds.summary: Four ways to make survivors scream: Face the Darkness on a timer, Infectious Fright on downs, Phantom Fear when they look at you and THWACK! on breaks, all but Infectious Fright with a short Aura read.
builds.details: When you damage a Survivor, Face the Darkness hexes them and lights a Dull Totem; until that Survivor is downed or healed, every {{Hex: Face the Darkness|screaminterval}} s the other Survivors outside your Terror Radius scream and you see their Auras for {{Hex: Face the Darkness|aurarevealduration}} s. Whenever a Survivor is downed, Infectious Fright makes Survivors in your Terror Radius scream and alerts you for {{Infectious Fright|revealduration}} s, and Phantom Fear makes a Survivor in your Terror Radius scream and show their Aura for {{Phantom Fear|aurarevealduration}} s when they look at you (cooldown {{Phantom Fear|cooldown}} s). THWACK! starts with {{THWACK!|startingtokens}} Tokens and earns one per hook (up to {{THWACK!|maxtokens}}); breaking a Pallet or Breakable Wall spends one to make all Survivors within {{THWACK!|range}} m scream and show their Auras for {{THWACK!|revealduration}} s. It is mostly a way to annoy the lobby, with short Aura reads as a bonus.
tips: Downing the hexed Survivor or letting them heal extinguishes Face the Darkness; damaging a Survivor again lights a new Dull Totem if one is left.
THWACK! runs dry after {{THWACK!|startingtokens}} breaks unless you hook in between.
Shown on The Animatronic; none of the perks depend on a killer power.

builds.title: Jumpscare Springtrap
builds.summary: Three Undetectable triggers (Unforeseen on kicks, Dark Devotion when the Obsession is hit, Furtive Chase when they are hooked) plus Third Seal's Blindness, for walking up on people.
builds.details: Whenever you damage a generator, Unforeseen moves your Terror Radius to that generator with a {{Unforeseen|terrorradiussize}} m radius and makes you Undetectable for {{Unforeseen|effectduration}} s (cooldown {{Unforeseen|cooldown}} s). Whenever the Obsession takes damage, Dark Devotion sets your Terror Radius to {{Dark Devotion|terrorradiussize}} m and gives it to the Obsession for {{Dark Devotion|terrorradiustransferduration}} s while you are Undetectable, and Furtive Chase gives you {{Furtive Chase|haste%}}% Haste and Undetectable for {{Furtive Chase|undetectablehasteduration}} s when you hook the Obsession, after which whoever unhooks them becomes the new Obsession. Hex: The Third Seal gives Blindness to Survivors you damage with a basic or special attack, up to {{Hex: The Third Seal|maxaffectedsurvivors}} Survivors, which stops them reading Auras. It is built for jumpscares rather than wins.
tips: Hit the Obsession first: Dark Devotion hands them your Terror Radius, so it follows them instead of you.
Furtive Chase passes the Obsession to whoever unhooks them, which gives Dark Devotion a new target.
Unforeseen leaves your Terror Radius at the kicked generator while you walk away Undetectable.

builds.title: Jumpscare Dredge
builds.summary: Find survivors with Discordance and Barbecue & Chili, then approach while Undetectable from Trail of Torment or Tinkerer.
builds.details: Discordance alerts you whenever a generator within {{Discordance|effectrange}} m is being repaired by at least {{Discordance|survivorsneeded}} Survivors and shows its Aura as long as at least {{Discordance|survivorsneeded}} keep repairing it (plus {{Discordance|auralingerduration}} s), and for {{Barbecue & Chili|aurarevealduration}} s after each hook, Barbecue & Chili shows Survivors at least {{Barbecue & Chili|mindistancefromhook}} m from the hooked one. Trail of Torment makes you Undetectable after you damage a generator until it stops regressing (cooldown {{Trail of Torment|cooldown}} s), though Survivors see that generator's Aura, and Tinkerer alerts you and makes you Undetectable for {{Tinkerer|undetectableduration}} s the first time each generator reaches {{Tinkerer|triggerthreshold%}}% progress. On The Dredge, the aim is to show up next to those Survivors with no warning; the build comes from a video about bringing the horror back to the game.
tips: Tinkerer only triggers once per generator, at {{Tinkerer|triggerthreshold%}}% progress.
Trail of Torment shows the kicked generator to Survivors, so they know where you were.
Source is from November 2025; the descriptions here follow the current perk text.

builds.title: Undetectable Unknown
builds.summary: A stealth setup for The Unknown: Unforeseen and Furtive Chase give Undetectable, Discordance finds groups on generators and Alien Instinct marks the farthest injured Survivor after each hook.
builds.details: Whenever you damage a generator, Unforeseen makes you Undetectable for {{Unforeseen|effectduration}} s and moves your Terror Radius to that generator with a {{Unforeseen|terrorradiussize}} m radius (cooldown {{Unforeseen|cooldown}} s), and Furtive Chase gives you {{Furtive Chase|haste%}}% Haste and Undetectable for {{Furtive Chase|undetectablehasteduration}} s whenever you hook the Obsession. Whenever you hook a Survivor, Alien Instinct makes the farthest injured Survivor Oblivious for {{Alien Instinct|obliviousduration}} s and shows you their Aura for {{Alien Instinct|aurarevealduration}} s, and Discordance alerts you to any generator within {{Discordance|effectrange}} m being repaired by at least {{Discordance|survivorsneeded}} Survivors. An Oblivious Survivor does not perceive your Terror Radius, so Alien Instinct's target gets no Terror Radius warning from you. The point is to reach Survivors before they get any warning, for jumpscares rather than efficiency.
tips: Furtive Chase passes the Obsession to whoever unhooks them, so your next Obsession hook can be a different Survivor.
Kick a generator on your way to a group that Discordance found so Unforeseen hides your approach.
Source is from November 2025; the descriptions here follow the current perk text.

builds.title: Vault-Speed Killer
builds.summary: Four window-vault speed bonuses on one killer, and Bamboozle blocks each window you vault for survivors, one at a time.
builds.details: Bamboozle ({{Bamboozle|windowvaultspeed%}}%) and Dark Arrogance ({{Dark Arrogance|vaultspeedincrease%}}%) make your basic window vaults faster all match, and Fire Up adds {{Fire Up|actionspeedbonus%}}% per Token, earning one Token per completed generator up to {{Fire Up|maxtokens}}. Whenever a survivor medium- or fast-vaults within {{Superior Anatomy|survivorvaultdistance}} m of you, Superior Anatomy makes your window vaults {{Superior Anatomy|vaultspeed%}}% faster for {{Superior Anatomy|vaultspeedduration}} s the next time you vault one (cooldown {{Superior Anatomy|cooldown}} s). Vault speed is subject to diminishing returns, so the largest bonus counts in full and each further one counts for less. Each window you vault is blocked for survivors for {{Bamboozle|windowblockdurations}} s, one window at a time; the video plays it on The Shape, The Xenomorph and The Singularity.
tips: Older source (August 2025).
Dark Arrogance makes blinds and pallet stuns on you {{Dark Arrogance|extrablindstunduration%}}% longer, so respect pallets and flashlights.
Dark Arrogance also makes your missed basic-attack cooldown {{Dark Arrogance|attackcooldownreduction%}}% shorter.
Fire Up starts with no Tokens, so the build gets faster as survivors complete generators.

builds.title: Flashlight Punisher
builds.summary: Shadowborn gives Haste when you are blinded, and Rampage gives Haste when you are blinded or pallet-stunned, scaling with each pallet or wall you have broken.
builds.details: Each pallet or breakable wall you basic-break earns a Rampage Token (up to {{Rampage|tokensmaximum}}), and Brutal Strength breaks them {{Brutal Strength|actionspeed%}}% faster. Whenever you are blinded or pallet-stunned, Rampage gives {{Rampage|hastevalue}}% Haste per Token for {{Rampage|hasteduration}} s (cooldown {{Rampage|cooldown}} s), and a blind also gives Shadowborn's {{Shadowborn|haste%}}% Haste for {{Shadowborn|duration}} s; Haste from several perks adds up, subject to diminishing returns. Once you have hooked {{Hex: Scared to Death|uniquesurvivorstohook}} different survivors, Hex: Scared to Death lights a Dull Totem, and from then on each pallet you basic-break while chasing makes survivors within {{Hex: Scared to Death|distancetosurvivors}} m scream and gain {{Hex: Scared to Death|hinderedvalue}}% Hindered for {{Hex: Scared to Death|hinderedduration}} s.
tips: Shown on The Dredge, The Ghost Face, The Wraith and The Legion.
Break pallets early: Rampage's Haste on a blind or stun scales with how many pallets and walls you have already broken.
Hex: Scared to Death needs a Dull Totem still standing when it lights, and it ends if survivors cleanse that totem.

builds.title: Phantom Terror Radius
builds.summary: Three perks move your terror radius away from you while you are Undetectable, so survivors hear a heartbeat where you are not.
builds.details: Whenever the Obsession takes damage, for {{Dark Devotion|terrorradiustransferduration}} s Dark Devotion sets your Terror Radius to {{Dark Devotion|terrorradiussize}} m, gives it to the Obsession and makes you Undetectable. Whenever you damage a generator, Unforeseen moves your Terror Radius onto that generator with a {{Unforeseen|terrorradiussize}} m radius and makes you Undetectable for {{Unforeseen|effectduration}} s (cooldown {{Unforeseen|cooldown}} s). Hex: Overture of Doom hexes the generator farthest from its totem; after a survivor repairs it for {{Hex: Overture of Doom|requiredtime}} s, your Terror Radius is set to that generator and you are Undetectable for {{Hex: Overture of Doom|terrorradiusdisplacementduration}} s, and once it is repaired the next farthest generator is hexed. Gearhead adds information: for {{Gearhead|effectduration}} s after any survivor takes damage, a survivor who hits a good basic skill check while repairing shows you their aura for {{Gearhead|aurarevealduration}} s.
tips: Demonstrated on The Unknown, The Singularity and The Animatronic.
Kick a generator before you leave it: Unforeseen leaves your heartbeat there while you move on Undetectable.
Undetectable from several of these perks does not stack; overlapping timers only matter for how long you stay hidden.
Hex: Overture of Doom ends if survivors cleanse its totem.

builds.title: Haste Ambush Pig
builds.summary: Four conditional Haste perks on The Pig, triggered by finished generators, compromised generators, Obsession hooks and window vaults after an injury.
builds.details: Batteries Included gives {{Batteries Included|haste%}}% Haste within {{Batteries Included|requireddistance}} m of a completed generator, ending {{Batteries Included|hastelingerduration}} s after you leave. Every generator you damage becomes compromised under Machine Learning (up to {{Machine Learning|generatorscompromised}}), and when survivors complete one you gain {{Machine Learning|haste%}}% Haste and Undetectable for {{Machine Learning|perkduration}} s. Hooking the Obsession gives Furtive Chase's {{Furtive Chase|haste%}}% Haste and Undetectable for {{Furtive Chase|undetectablehasteduration}} s, and whoever unhooks the Obsession becomes the new one. For {{Unbound|effectduration}} s after a healthy survivor is injured, each window you basic-vault gives Unbound's {{Unbound|haste%}}% Haste for {{Unbound|hasteduration}} s; the video stacks all of this for long-range ambushes.
tips: The creator lists Play With Your Food or Knock Out as alternatives to Unbound.
Video add-ons: Last Will and Workshop Grease.
Haste from several perks adds up, but diminishing returns make each extra source count for less than its listed value.
When survivors complete one compromised generator, Machine Learning clears the others, so kick new generators again afterwards.

builds.title: Pallet Shredder Springtrap
builds.summary: Shorter pallet stuns, faster pallet breaks, and Exposed for any survivor who stuns you.
builds.details: Enduring makes pallet stuns {{Enduring|stundurationreduction%}}% shorter while you are not carrying a survivor, and Hubris makes any survivor who stuns you Exposed for {{Hubris|exposedduration}} s (cooldown {{Hubris|cooldown}} s). Brutal Strength breaks pallets and breakable walls {{Brutal Strength|actionspeed%}}% faster, and Fire Up adds {{Fire Up|actionspeedbonus%}}% per Token, earning one Token per completed generator up to {{Fire Up|maxtokens}}; break speed is subject to diminishing returns, so the smaller of the two bonuses counts for less. A pallet stun costs you less time, the pallet is gone quickly, and the survivor who stunned you is Exposed.
tips: Enduring does nothing while you carry a survivor, so pallet stuns during a carry are full length.
Hubris has a {{Hubris|cooldown}} s cooldown, so a second stun within {{Hubris|cooldown}} s of the first does not apply Exposed.
Brutal Strength and Fire Up also make you damage generators faster.

builds.title: 2016 Throwback Meta
builds.summary: The oldest loadout in the video's tour of past killer metas: tracking, pallet breaking, fast carries and an endgame Hex, replayed in 2026.
builds.details: Whispers makes you hear whispers at random while you are within {{Whispers|rangetosurvivors}} m of a survivor and gives you {{Whispers|hasteamount%}}% Haste while you are farther than that from survivors. Brutal Strength breaks pallets and breakable walls and damages generators {{Brutal Strength|actionspeed%}}% faster, and Agitation gives you {{Agitation|haste%}}% Haste and a {{Agitation|terrorradiusincreasesize}} m larger Terror Radius while you carry a survivor. When all generators are completed, Hex: No One Escapes Death lights a Dull Totem that makes survivors Exposed and gives you {{Hex: No One Escapes Death|haste%}}% Haste; survivors within {{Hex: No One Escapes Death|aurarevealstartrange}} m see its totem's aura, a range that grows to {{Hex: No One Escapes Death|aurarevealendrange}} m over {{Hex: No One Escapes Death|aurasizeincreasedelay}} s. The video replays several historical metas to see how they fare now.
tips: No One Escapes Death needs a Dull Totem left when the last generator is completed; if survivors have cleansed them all, it cannot light.
Hearing Whispers tells you a survivor is within {{Whispers|rangetosurvivors}} m of you.
Agitation's larger terror radius while carrying gives survivors near your route more warning.

builds.title: The Stealth Build
builds.summary: One generator kick can set off Nowhere to Hide's reveal of Survivors within {{Nowhere to Hide|aurarevealdistance}} m, Trail of Torment's Undetectable and Dragon's Grip's Exposed trap; kick soon after a hook and Pop Goes the Weasel adds extra regression.
builds.details: Whenever you damage a generator, Nowhere to Hide shows you the auras of survivors within {{Nowhere to Hide|aurarevealdistance}} m of it for {{Nowhere to Hide|aurarevealduration}} s, and Trail of Torment makes you Undetectable until that generator stops regressing, although survivors see the generator's aura meanwhile (cooldown {{Trail of Torment|cooldown}} s). The same kick arms Dragon's Grip on that generator for {{Dragon’s Grip|activeduration}} s: the first survivor to repair it screams, you are alerted to their position for {{Dragon’s Grip|aurarevealduration}} s, and they are Exposed for {{Dragon’s Grip|exposedduration}} s (cooldown {{Dragon’s Grip|cooldown}} s). Pop Goes the Weasel adds to the hook: for {{Pop Goes the Weasel|activeduration}} s after each hook, when you damage a generator it explodes and loses {{Pop Goes the Weasel|extrageneratordamage%}}% more progress. Game Rant builds it around kicking a generator, staying hidden nearby and ambushing whoever comes back.
tips: Article last updated October 2024; all four perks still exist.
Pop Goes the Weasel only works for {{Pop Goes the Weasel|activeduration}} s after a hook, so head from the hook straight to a generator and kick it.
Survivors can see the generator you kicked while Trail of Torment is active; wait nearby, because the first one to repair it triggers Dragon's Grip.
Trail of Torment and Dragon's Grip each have a cooldown ({{Trail of Torment|cooldown}} s for Trail of Torment, {{Dragon’s Grip|cooldown}} s for Dragon's Grip), so not every kick triggers them.

builds.title: Speed Ghostie
builds.summary: Haste from the Obsession, finished generators and compromised generators, plus longer lunges after each completed generator, on The Ghost Face.
builds.details: Play With Your Food earns a Token each time you stop chasing the Obsession (up to {{Play With Your Food|maxtokens}}, cooldown {{Play With Your Food|chargegainedcooldown}} s) and gives {{Play With Your Food|haste%}}% Haste per Token, but every attack costs one Token. Batteries Included adds {{Batteries Included|haste%}}% Haste within {{Batteries Included|requireddistance}} m of a completed generator, and Machine Learning gives {{Machine Learning|haste%}}% Haste and Undetectable for {{Machine Learning|perkduration}} s when survivors complete a compromised generator, which is one you damaged. Each completed generator also earns {{Coup de Grâce|tokensgainedpergenerator}} Coup de Grâce Tokens (up to {{Coup de Grâce|maxtokens}}), and every lunge attack spends one to make it {{Coup de Grâce|lungeextraduration%}}% longer.
tips: Older source (November 2025).
Video add-ons: Drop-Leg Knife Sheath and "Caught on Tape".
Stop chasing the Obsession a few times before going for the hit: each stop earns a Play With Your Food Token (cooldown {{Play With Your Food|chargegainedcooldown}} s), and each attack loses one.
Every lunge attack spends a Coup de Grâce Token automatically, so you cannot choose which lunge gets the extra reach; Tokens build up to {{Coup de Grâce|maxtokens}} as generators are completed.

builds.title: Vanishing Act
builds.summary: Sprint Burst gets you away, Ghost Notes and Lightweight shorten your scratch marks, and Parental Guidance hides your trail after you stun the killer.
builds.details: Sprint Burst gives {{Sprint Burst|haste%}}% Haste for {{Sprint Burst|hasteduration}} s and {{Sprint Burst|exhaustionduration}} s of Exhausted whenever you start running. While you are Exhausted, Ghost Notes makes your scratch marks disappear {{Ghost Notes|scratchmarkstimereduction%}}% faster, and it also makes you lose Exhausted {{Ghost Notes|cooldownreduction%}}% faster. Lightweight always makes your scratch marks disappear {{Lightweight|scratchmarkstimereduction}} s faster and appear more spread out, and whenever you stun the killer, Parental Guidance removes your scratch marks, pools of blood and grunts of pain for {{Parental Guidance|stealthduration}} s.
tips: Seine pairs it with a Fog Vial.
A teammate variant swaps in Boon: Dark Theory and Boon: Shadow Step.
Sprint Burst triggers as soon as you start running while not Exhausted, so walk until you need it.
Parental Guidance needs you to stun the killer yourself, for example with a pallet.

builds.title: Vault-Speed Parkour
builds.summary: Fast, silent vaults that end in a burst of Haste and leave no scratch marks behind you.
builds.details: Finesse makes your fast vaults {{Finesse|vaultspeedincrease%}}% faster while you are healthy (cooldown {{Finesse|cooldown}} s after each fast vault), and Lithe gives {{Lithe|haste%}}% Haste for {{Lithe|hasteduration}} s and {{Lithe|exhaustionduration}} s of Exhausted on a medium or fast vault. Quick & Quiet makes the vault silent so the killer is not alerted (cooldown {{Quick & Quiet|cooldown}} s), and Dance With Me leaves no scratch marks for {{Dance With Me|duration}} s after a medium or fast vault (cooldown {{Dance With Me|cooldown}} s), so the killer often cannot tell which way you went.
tips: Same loadout appears in Game Rant's fun survivor builds list (https://gamerant.com/dead-by-daylight-fun-survivor-builds/).
Lithe cannot trigger while you are Exhausted, so vaults during that time give no Haste.
Finesse only works while you are healthy.
Quick & Quiet also makes hiding in lockers silent, and Dance With Me also triggers on a fast locker exit.

builds.title: Treasure Hunter
builds.summary: Find chests, open them fast, rummage empty ones again and loot items that come with add-ons.
builds.details: Plunderer's Instinct shows you the auras of chests and items, unlocks chests {{Plunderer's Instinct|actionspeed%}}% faster and makes a higher-rarity item {{Plunderer's Instinct|modifychestrarity}}% more likely when you unlock one. Appraisal starts you with {{Appraisal|startingtokens}} Tokens, each spent to rummage a chest that is already empty, up to {{Appraisal|maxrummagesperchest}} times per chest, and you rummage chests {{Appraisal|chestsearchspeedbonus%}}% faster. Every item you loot from a chest gets a Visceral-or-lower add-on from Ace in the Hole, with a {{Ace in the Hole|modifychestitemsecondaddonchance%}}% chance of a second Uncommon-or-lower one, and you keep your add-ons if you escape. After you have rummaged or unlocked a chest, Moment of Glory makes you Broken when you are injured while not Broken, then heals you instantly {{Moment of Glory|timetoheal}} s later if you have not been downed.
tips: Open a chest early: Moment of Glory does nothing until you have rummaged or unlocked one.
Appraisal's Tokens are only for rummaging empty chests, so save them for chests someone has already opened.

builds.title: Totem Hunter
builds.summary: Find totems and cleanse them quickly, cash in a cleanse for a locker heal, and once you have also opened a chest, turn your screams into killer aura reads.
builds.details: Whenever a generator is completed, Detective's Hunch shows you chests, generators and totems within {{Detective's Hunch|revealdistance}} m for {{Detective's Hunch|revealduration}} s. Counterforce starts you with {{Counterforce|startingtokens}} Token and earns another per cleanse, each making cleansing {{Counterforce|stackablecleansespeed%}}% faster, and every cleanse shows you the aura of the farthest totem for {{Counterforce|aurarevealduration}} s. After a cleanse, Inner Strength makes you healthy once you have hidden in a locker for {{Inner Strength|hideduration}} s while injured and not Broken. Once you have cleansed or blessed a totem and unlocked a chest, Hardened shows you the killer's aura for {{Hardened|aurarevealduration}} s instead of each scream.
tips: Hardened needs a chest unlocked as well as a totem, and Detective's Hunch shows you nearby chests.
Cleansing a Hex totem removes that Hex, so the build is a counter to Hex-heavy killers.
Inner Strength does not work while you are Broken.

builds.title: Wallhacks Build
builds.summary: Killer aura reads when you start each new generator, when a generator is completed and when you are unhooked, plus Dark Sense when the killer comes close after a completion, all made longer by Eyes of Belmont.
builds.details: Poised shows the killer's aura for {{Poised|aurarevealduration}} s the first time you start repairing each generator, and Eyes of Belmont shows it for {{Eyes of Belmont|aurarevealduration}} s whenever a generator is completed. After a generator is completed, Dark Sense triggers when the killer comes within {{Dark Sense|killerrange}} m of you and shows you the killer, the other survivors, and pallets and windows within {{Dark Sense|aurarange}} m for {{Dark Sense|effectduration}} s. Wicked shows the killer's aura for {{Wicked|aurarevealduration}} s whenever you are unhooked and lets you unhook yourself in the basement, and Eyes of Belmont adds {{Eyes of Belmont|aurarevealbonusduration}} s to every timed killer aura read you get. Game Rant pairs the build with a key and an aura add-on.
tips: Poised only triggers the first time you start repairing each generator, so starting repairs on new generators gives more reads.
Poised also leaves no scratch marks for {{Poised|stealthduration}} s whenever a generator is completed.
If the killer's power or perks make them Undetectable, these reads do not show them.

builds.title: Locker Build
builds.summary: Lockers do everything: hide in them silently, heal in them after a cleanse, and jump out of them to stun the killer.
builds.details: Quick & Quiet makes hiding in a locker silent so the killer is not alerted (cooldown {{Quick & Quiet|cooldown}} s). After you have hidden for {{Head On|hiderequiredduration}} s, Head On lets you fast-exit to stun the killer for {{Head On|lockerstunduration}} s if they are within {{Head On|lockerstunrange}} m, after which you are Exhausted for {{Head On|exhaustedduration}} s, and Dance With Me leaves no scratch marks for {{Dance With Me|duration}} s after a fast exit (cooldown {{Dance With Me|cooldown}} s). Inner Strength turns a cleansed totem into a heal: while you are injured and not Broken, hiding in a locker for {{Inner Strength|hideduration}} s makes you healthy instantly.
tips: Head On cannot be used while you are Exhausted, and the stun only lands if the killer is within {{Head On|lockerstunrange}} m when you jump out.
Cleanse a totem before you need a heal so Inner Strength is ready.
Quick & Quiet also makes your vaults silent.

builds.title: The Luck Build
builds.summary: Leave the match to the dice: Dramaturgy's random outcome, Bardic Inspiration's d20 for team skill checks, and Up the Ante's luck and self-unhooks for everyone.
builds.details: While healthy and running, press the Active Ability button for Dramaturgy: you get {{Dramaturgy|haste%}}% Haste for {{Dramaturgy|hasteduration}} s and {{Dramaturgy|exhaustionduration}} s of Exhausted, then a random result (more Haste, Exposed for {{Dramaturgy|exposedduration}} s, a random rare item with add-ons, or a scream that does nothing), never the same one twice in a row. While idle, press the Active Ability button to perform Bardic Inspiration for up to {{Bardic Inspiration|performanceduration}} s for survivors within {{Bardic Inspiration|performancedistance}} m (others see your aura meanwhile); a d20 roll sets the bonus progress their basic skill checks give, from +{{Bardic Inspiration|lowrollbonus%}}% to +{{Bardic Inspiration|highrollbonus%}}% or nothing on the lowest roll, for {{Bardic Inspiration|effectduration}} s if you complete the performance (cooldown {{Bardic Inspiration|cooldown}} s). Up the Ante makes all survivors {{Up the Ante|luckincrease%}}% luckier for each other survivor alive and lets every survivor attempt to unhook themselves. Slippery Meat is the one sure thing: other survivors unhook you faster and you gain {{Slippery Meat|unhookhastebonus}}% more Haste when unhooked.
tips: Article last updated December 2024; perk effects have since been adjusted, but all four perks still exist.
Slippery Meat's current text has no luck effect: other survivors unhook you faster and you gain more Haste when unhooked.
Dramaturgy cannot be used while you are Exhausted, and the lowest Bardic Inspiration roll just makes you scream.

builds.title: The Deception Build
builds.summary: Four ways to send the killer somewhere you are not: a fake survivor, a thrown pebble, a generator alert from a locker and a fake locker entry.
builds.details: Once you have repaired {{Mirrored Illusion|requiredprogress%}}% of generators, press the Secondary Ability button next to a chest, exit gate switch, generator or totem to leave a static illusion for {{Mirrored Illusion|huskduration}} s with Mirrored Illusion. Diversion charges after you hide for {{Diversion|requiredchargetime}} s inside the killer's terror radius; then, crouched and idle, press the Active Ability button to throw a pebble {{Diversion|throwdistance}} m away that alerts the killer and leaves scratch marks. With Red Herring, after you repair a generator for at least {{Red Herring|timetoactivate}} s you see its aura, and hiding in a locker alerts the killer to that generator (cooldown {{Red Herring|cooldown}} s). Deception turns an attempted fast locker entry into a fake: you stay outside, the killer is alerted, and you leave no scratch marks or pools of blood for {{Deception|noscratchmarksduration}} s (cooldown {{Deception|cooldown}} s).
tips: Article last updated December 2024.
Charge Diversion while the killer is close but not chasing you: it needs time spent hiding inside the terror radius.
None of these perks speed up repairs, and Mirrored Illusion and Red Herring both need you to repair generators yourself.

builds.title: The Trap Build
builds.summary: Booby-trap generators and pallets: Blast Mine and Wiretap go on generators, Chemical Trap on a dropped pallet, and Any Means Necessary stands pallets back up.
builds.details: Once you have repaired {{Blast Mine|requiredprogress%}}% of generators, press the Secondary Ability button next to a generator to trap it with Blast Mine for {{Blast Mine|trapduration}} s; if the killer damages it, they are stunned for {{Blast Mine|stunblindduration}} s and everyone nearby looking at the detonation is blinded. Once you have repaired {{Wiretap|requiredprogress%}}% of generators, Wiretap traps a generator the same way for {{Wiretap|trapduration}} s or until the killer damages it, and while the killer is within {{Wiretap|aurarevealrange}} m of it all survivors see the killer's aura. Once you have repaired {{Chemical Trap|requiredprogress%}}% of generators, press the Secondary Ability button next to a dropped pallet to trap it with Chemical Trap for {{Chemical Trap|trapduration}} s; the killer who breaks it gains {{Chemical Trap|hinder%}}% Hindered for {{Chemical Trap|hinderduration}} s. Any Means Necessary shows you dropped pallets and lets you stand one back up by using the Active Ability button next to it for {{Any Means Necessary|actiontimerequired}} s.
tips: Article last updated December 2024.
Every trap shows its generator or pallet to all survivors while it is armed.
Any Means Necessary has no repair requirement, so you can use it on dropped pallets from the start of the match.

builds.title: No Mither Hard Mode
builds.summary: Start the trial injured and Broken with No Mither, then rely on Decisive Strike and Lithe to survive it.
builds.details: No Mither makes you injured and Broken from the start, but your grunts of pain are {{No Mither|injuredvoicelevelreduction%}}% quieter, you leave no pools of blood, and you recover {{No Mither|extrarecover%}}% faster and can fully recover. Object of Obsession and Decisive Strike both make you more likely to start as the Obsession; while you are, the killer sees your aura for {{Object of Obsession|aurarevealduration}} s every {{Object of Obsession|revealtimeintervals}} s, and during each reveal you see theirs and repair, heal and cleanse {{Object of Obsession|actionspeedbonus%}}% faster. Decisive Strike stuns the killer for {{Decisive Strike|stunduration}} s if you hit its special skill check when picked up within {{Decisive Strike|effectduration}} s of an unhook (once per trial, until all generators are completed), and Lithe gives {{Lithe|haste%}}% Haste for {{Lithe|hasteduration}} s on a medium or fast vault. Game Rant pitches escaping with it as the ultimate challenge.
tips: Article last updated December 2024.
Decisive Strike is disabled by conspicuous actions, so avoid them in the {{Decisive Strike|effectduration}} s after an unhook if you want to keep it.
Lithe gives you {{Lithe|exhaustionduration}} s of Exhausted, and it cannot trigger again until that wears off.

builds.title: Basement Dweller
builds.summary: Turn a basement hook into a self-rescue: unhook yourself, heal on the spot, and see the killer's aura on the way out.
builds.details: In the basement, Wicked lets you unhook yourself, and every unhook shows you the killer's aura for {{Wicked|aurarevealduration}} s. Resurgence gives you {{Resurgence|healregain%}}% healing progress whenever you are unhooked, and Strength in Shadows lets you heal yourself in the basement at {{Strength in Shadows|selfhealspeed%}}% slower speed, showing you the killer's aura for {{Strength in Shadows|aurarevealduration}} s when you finish healing. Decisive Strike covers the exit: if the killer picks you up within {{Decisive Strike|effectduration}} s of an unhook, hitting its special skill check stuns them for {{Decisive Strike|stunduration}} s (once per trial, until all generators are completed). Tatariu describes it as the best survivor build nobody is using.
tips: Older source (May 2025).
Wicked's self-unhook and Strength in Shadows' self-heal only work while you are in the basement.

builds.title: Speed Build
builds.summary: Stack survivor Haste: Power of Two after you finish healing a teammate, Dark Theory near your Boon, and Hope once the generators are done.
builds.details: While healthy and healing another survivor without a Med-Kit, press the Active Ability button for For the People to heal them instantly, at the cost of taking damage, {{For the People|brokenduration}} s of Broken and becoming the Obsession. Separately, whenever you finish healing another survivor, Teamwork: Power of Two gives you both {{Teamwork: Power of Two|haste%}}% Haste while you stay within {{Teamwork: Power of Two|requireddistance}} m of each other, ending {{Teamwork: Power of Two|lingerduration}} s after either of you leaves that range. Once you bless a totem with the Active Ability button, Boon: Dark Theory gives {{Boon: Dark Theory|haste%}}% Haste to survivors in that Boon totem's range, lingering {{Boon: Dark Theory|lingerduration}} s after they leave, and Hope adds {{Hope|haste%}}% Haste once all generators are completed. Haste from several perks adds up, but diminishing returns make each extra source count for less.
tips: The teammate in the video swaps For the People for Blood Pact.
For the People makes you take damage and gives you {{For the People|brokenduration}} s of Broken, so use it only when an instant heal is worth that price.
All your Boons share the one totem you bless, so if the killer snuffs it, Dark Theory's Haste is gone until you bless another.

builds.title: Flashbang Vanish
builds.summary: Stun the killer and Parental Guidance hides your trail; Decisive Strike supplies a stun, and a Flashbang crafted in a locker buys another escape.
builds.details: Whenever you stun the killer, Parental Guidance removes your scratch marks, pools of blood and grunts of pain for {{Parental Guidance|stealthduration}} s, and Iron Will keeps your grunts of pain {{Iron Will|injurednoisereduction%}}% quieter while you are injured and not Exhausted. Decisive Strike gives you a stun to set it off: if the killer picks you up within {{Decisive Strike|effectduration}} s of an unhook, hitting its special skill check stuns them for {{Decisive Strike|stunduration}} s (once per trial, until all generators are completed). Once you have repaired {{Flashbang|requiredprogresstocraft%}}% of generators, use the Active Ability button while hiding in a locker to craft a Flashbang, which blinds everyone nearby looking at the detonation and alerts the killer. A blind is not a stun, so the Flashbang alone does not trigger Parental Guidance.
tips: Seine suggests a toolbox to reach the Flashbang repair threshold quickly.
Pallet stuns also trigger Parental Guidance, so you are not limited to Decisive Strike.
Decisive Strike is disabled by conspicuous actions, so avoid them in the {{Decisive Strike|effectduration}} s after an unhook if you want to keep it.

builds.title: Pure Evil Blast Mine
builds.summary: Mine a generator with Blast Mine, then use a fake survivor, thrown pebbles and fake locker entries to lure the killer over to kick it.
builds.details: Once you have repaired {{Blast Mine|requiredprogress%}}% of generators, press the Secondary Ability button next to a generator to trap it with Blast Mine for {{Blast Mine|trapduration}} s; all survivors see its aura, and if the killer damages it they are stunned for {{Blast Mine|stunblindduration}} s and everyone nearby looking at the detonation is blinded. Mirrored Illusion leaves a static illusion next to a generator, chest, exit gate switch or totem for {{Mirrored Illusion|huskduration}} s, Diversion lets you throw a pebble {{Diversion|throwdistance}} m that alerts the killer and leaves scratch marks, and Deception alerts the killer with a fake fast locker entry. The creator plays it purely to troll the killer.
tips: Older source (November 2025).

Mirrored Illusion and Blast Mine need you to have repaired {{Mirrored Illusion|requiredprogress%}}% and {{Blast Mine|requiredprogress%}}% of generators first; Diversion and Deception have no repair requirement.
Diversion needs {{Diversion|requiredchargetime}} s of hiding inside the terror radius before you can throw it.

builds.title: Easy-Mode Looper
builds.summary: A relaxed chase build: silent footsteps, faster fast vaults, killer reads on pallet drops and faster repairs for teammates while you are chased.
builds.details: While you are healthy and running, Light-footed makes your footsteps silent to the killer (cooldown {{Light-footed|cooldown}} s after each fast action), and Finesse makes your fast vaults {{Finesse|vaultspeedincrease%}}% faster while healthy (cooldown {{Finesse|cooldown}} s after each one). While you are chased, Troubleshooter shows you the generator with the most progress and the killer's aura for {{Troubleshooter|aurarevealduration}} s whenever you drop a pallet, lasting {{Troubleshooter|lingeringduration}} s after the chase ends. Quick Gambit makes other survivors repair {{Quick Gambit|repairboost%}}% faster and shows you their auras while you are chased, but it goes on a {{Quick Gambit|cooldown}} s cooldown whenever you take damage. Tatariu pitches it as an easy way to keep the killer busy in a long chase.
tips: Older source (March 2025).
Light-footed and Finesse only work while you are healthy, so the build is strongest before your first hit.

builds.title: Endgame Clutch
builds.summary: Nothing happens until the last generator is completed, then all four perks switch on: a heal, Haste, faster gates and faster rescues.
builds.details: When all generators are completed, Adrenaline heals you instantly if you are injured or downed and then, ignoring Exhausted, gives {{Adrenaline|haste%}}% Haste for {{Adrenaline|hasteduration}} s and {{Adrenaline|exhaustionduration}} s of Exhausted, while Hope gives you {{Hope|haste%}}% Haste. Wake Up! shows you the exit gate switches and makes you open exit gates {{Wake Up!|gateopenspeedself%}}% faster, plus {{Wake Up!|gateopenspeedother%}}% for each other survivor alive, while other survivors see your aura as you open one. No One Left Behind lets you heal other survivors {{No One Left Behind|actionspeed%}}% faster and unhook them {{No One Left Behind|unhookspeed%}}% faster, shows you their auras, and gives each survivor you unhook {{No One Left Behind|increasedhaste%}}% more Haste. Seine uses it to rescue teammates in the endgame.
tips: Older source (January 2025).
None of the four perks do anything before the last generator is completed, so the early game is up to you.
